368.title: Connexions
368.content: Meshtastic supports multiple transport methods to communicate between your phone or desktop and a node.

369.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
369.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Icon | State | Description | . | 🟢 | Connecté | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Connexion en cours | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Déconnecté | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Appareil en veille | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Bluetooth | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Réseau | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Troubleshooting Bluetooth . | Node not found: Turn Bluetooth off and back on. On Android 11 and older, also check that system location services are switched on. Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. A node that keeps failing here is usually crashing on reconnect. Power-cycle the node, then tap it again on the Connect tab to start a fresh attempt. | .

370.title: USB Serial
370.content: USB connections provide a wired alternative, useful for desktop or when Bluetooth is unavailable. Setup . | Connect your node to your phone with a USB data cable. Charge-only cables carry no data lines, and a node on one never appears in the list. | The app prompts for USB permission. Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. Troubleshooting USB . | USB permission denied: Unplug the node and plug it back in. Android asks again on reconnect. | No node in the list: Check that the cable carries data rather than only power, and that the phone supports OTG. | .

371.title: TCP/IP (Network)
371.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . Approvisionnement Wi-Fi pour mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

372.title: After Your First Connection
372.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

373.title: Live Update
373.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

374.title: Reconnection Behavior
374.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

375.title: Quick Settings Tile
375.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

376.title: Desktop Connections
376.content: On Desktop (Linux/macOS/Windows), the app supports: . | Bluetooth (BLE) — via the Kable library; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows | USB Serial — primary wired connection method | TCP/IP — for network-connected nodes | . See Desktop App for platform-specific details and keyboard shortcuts.

396.title: Connections
396.content: Meshtastic supports multiple transport methods to communicate between your phone or desktop and a node.

397.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
397.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Icon | State | Popis | . | 🟢 | Pripojený | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Prebieha pripájanie | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Odpojené | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Vysielač uspaný | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Bluetooth | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Sieť | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Troubleshooting Bluetooth . | Node not found: Turn Bluetooth off and back on. On Android 11 and older, also check that system location services are switched on. Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. A node that keeps failing here is usually crashing on reconnect. Power-cycle the node, then tap it again on the Connect tab to start a fresh attempt. | .

398.title: USB Serial
398.content: USB connections provide a wired alternative, useful for desktop or when Bluetooth is unavailable. Setup . | Connect your node to your phone with a USB data cable. Charge-only cables carry no data lines, and a node on one never appears in the list. | The app prompts for USB permission. Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. Troubleshooting USB . | USB permission denied: Unplug the node and plug it back in. Android asks again on reconnect. | No node in the list: Check that the cable carries data rather than only power, and that the phone supports OTG. | .

399.title: TCP/IP (Network)
399.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

400.title: After Your First Connection
400.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

401.title: Live Update
401.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

402.title: Reconnection Behavior
402.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

403.title: Quick Settings Tile
403.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

421.title: Live Update

The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. 422.title: Reconnection Behavior

Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. 450.title: After Your First Connection
450.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

451.title: Live Update
451.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

452.title: Uudelleenyhdistämisen toiminta
452.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

453.title: Quick Settings Tile
453.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

476.title: Connections
476.content: Meshtastic supports multiple transport methods to communicate between your phone or desktop and a node.

477.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
477.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Иконица | State | Опис | . | 🟢 | Блутут повезан | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Connecting | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Раскачено | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Уређај је у стању спавања | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Блутут | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Мрежа | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Troubleshooting Bluetooth . | Node not found: Turn Bluetooth off and back on. On Android 11 and older, also check that system location services are switched on. Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. A node that keeps failing here is usually crashing on reconnect. Power-cycle the node, then tap it again on the Connect tab to start a fresh attempt. | .

478.title: USB Serial
478.content: USB connections provide a wired alternative, useful for desktop or when Bluetooth is unavailable. Setup . | Connect your node to your phone with a USB data cable. Charge-only cables carry no data lines, and a node on one never appears in the list. | The app prompts for USB permission. Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. Troubleshooting USB . | USB permission denied: Unplug the node and plug it back in. Android asks again on reconnect. | No node in the list: Check that the cable carries data rather than only power, and that the phone supports OTG. | .

479.title: TCP/IP (Network)
479.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

480.title: After Your First Connection
480.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

481.title: Live Update
481.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

482.title: Reconnection Behavior
482.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

483.title: Quick Settings Tile
483.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

484.title: Desktop Connections
484.content: On Desktop (Linux/macOS/Windows), the app supports: . | Bluetooth (BLE) — via the Kable library; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows | USB Serial — primary wired connection method | TCP/IP — for network-connected nodes | . See Desktop App for platform-specific details and keyboard shortcuts.

503.title: Quick Settings Tile

Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. 506.title: Connections
506.content: Meshtastic supports multiple transport methods to communicate between your phone or desktop and a node.

507.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
507.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Icon | State | Cur síos | . | 🟢 | Connected | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Connecting | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Na ceangailte | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Gléas ina chodladh | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Bluetooth | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Network | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Troubleshooting Bluetooth . | Node not found: Turn Bluetooth off and back on. On Android 11 and older, also check that system location services are switched on. Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. A node that keeps failing here is usually crashing on reconnect. Power-cycle the node, then tap it again on the Connect tab to start a fresh attempt. | .

508.title: USB Serial
508.content: USB connections provide a wired alternative, useful for desktop or when Bluetooth is unavailable. Setup . | Connect your node to your phone with a USB data cable. Charge-only cables carry no data lines, and a node on one never appears in the list. | The app prompts for USB permission. Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. Troubleshooting USB . | USB permission denied: Unplug the node and plug it back in. Android asks again on reconnect. | No node in the list: Check that the cable carries data rather than only power, and that the phone supports OTG. | .

509.title: TCP/IP (Network)
509.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

510.title: After Your First Connection
510.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

530.title: After Your First Connection
530.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

531.title: Live Update
531.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

532.title: Reconnection Behavior
532.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

533.title: Quick Settings Tile
533.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

537.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
537.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Icon | State | Opis | . | 🟢 | Connected | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Connecting | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Odspojeno | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Uređaj je u stanju mirovanja | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Bluetooth | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Network | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. 558.title: USB Serial

Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. 559.title: TCP/IP (Network)
559.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

560.title: After Your First Connection
560.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

561.title: Live Update
561.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

562.title: Reconnection Behavior
562.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

563.title: Quick Settings Tile
563.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

564.content: On Desktop (Linux/macOS/Windows), the app supports: . | Bluetooth (BLE) — via the Kable library; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows | USB Serial — primary wired connection method | TCP/IP — for network-connected nodes | . 586.title: Verbindungen
586.content: Meshtastic supports multiple transport methods to communicate between your phone or desktop and a node.

587.title: Bluetooth (BLE)
587.content: Bluetooth Low Energy is the default and most common connection method on Android. Pairing a Radio . | Power on your node. Most nodes advertise over Bluetooth as soon as they boot, so there is no pairing mode to enter. Nodes with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth switched off, so turn it on from the node’s own on-screen menu first. | Open the app and navigate to the Connect tab. | Tap Scan for Bluetooth devices. Nearby Meshtastic nodes appear in the list. | Select your node from the list. | Android asks you to pair. If your node has a screen, it shows a six-digit PIN. Type that into the Android dialog. If your node has no screen, the PIN is 123456. | . To change the pairing method, or to turn Bluetooth on for a node that ships with it off, open Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth. See Settings — Radio & User. For more information, see Bluetooth configuration on meshtastic.org. Use the transport selector — a segmented button row below the connection card — to switch between the Bluetooth, Network, and USB transports (one is active at a time): . On hardware with no Bluetooth LE the selector leaves out Bluetooth, and on hardware with no USB host it leaves out USB. With Network as the only transport left, the selector is hidden. 💡 Tip: If your node doesn’t appear, check that it isn’t already connected to another phone, or out of range. The screen names anything on the app’s side that is blocking a scan, with the fix attached: . | What you see | What it means | . | A card asking for Nearby devices | The permission has not been granted. Grant permission requests it; once Android stops prompting, the button becomes Open settings. | . | Bluetooth is off | The adapter is disabled — the card opens Bluetooth settings. | . | Bluetooth scanning also needs location services | Android 11 and older only: the permission is held but the system location toggle is off. | . | No card, and No Bluetooth devices seen under the header | Nothing on this side is blocking the scan. The node is out of range, off, or already connected elsewhere. | . The explanation lives in that card, not in the scan control: tapping Scan for Bluetooth devices after you have declined once asks Android again directly. Connection Status . The Connect tab icon in the navigation bar shows the connection state by color: . | Symbol | Status | Beschreibung | . | 🟢 | Verbunden | Active link to the node. The badge shows the transport in use: Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or USB | . | 🟠 | Wird verbunden | Handshake in progress | . | 🔴 | Verbindung getrennt | No active connection. The app retries automatically, with a growing delay between attempts | . | 🟡 | Gerät schläft | The node is in light sleep. The app is waiting for it to wake and reconnect, not failing | . These are the four states the app models. “Device sleeping” is normal on power-saving configurations and needs no action. When connecting, a status indicator shows the current connection state — tap Stop Connecting to abandon the attempt: . Once connected, the connection card shows the node’s name and firmware version, its signal strength over Bluetooth, and its LoRa modem preset and region, for example “Long Range - Fast · United States”. A node on custom modem settings shows Custom in place of the preset. Tap the preset row to open the LoRa screen. With no node chosen yet, the connection card reads No device selected. A pane with nothing to list says so under its header, with a hint: . | Pane | What it shows | . | Bluetooth | No Bluetooth devices seen, and “Ensure you’re within range of the device.” Start a scan from the header. | . | Netzwerk | No network devices seen, and “Ensure you’re connected to the same network as the device.” Shown only while nothing has been discovered and Recent Network Devices is empty. Add device manually… stays below it. | . | USB | No USB devices detected, and “Connect a device with a USB data cable to use serial.” | . Troubleshooting Bluetooth . | Node not found: Turn Bluetooth off and back on. On Android 11 and older, also check that system location services are switched on. Those releases do not return scan results without them. | Bluetooth scan couldn’t start: Try again, and toggle Bluetooth off and on if it repeats. | Connection drops: Move closer to the node; check for interference. | Pairing failed, or pairing did not complete: Check that the Nearby devices permission is granted, then pair again. | Pairing rejected: Forget the device in Android Bluetooth settings and retry. | Could not establish a stable connection after repeated attempts: The app stopped retrying after three failed handshakes. A node that keeps failing here is usually crashing on reconnect. Power-cycle the node, then tap it again on the Connect tab to start a fresh attempt. | .

588.title: USB Serial
588.content: USB connections provide a wired alternative, useful for desktop or when Bluetooth is unavailable. Einstellungen . | Connect your node to your phone with a USB data cable. Charge-only cables carry no data lines, and a node on one never appears in the list. | The app prompts for USB permission. Tap Allow. | The connection is established automatically. | . ℹ️ Note: USB connections require OTG support on Android devices. Troubleshooting USB . | USB permission denied: Unplug the node and plug it back in. Android asks again on reconnect. | No node in the list: Check that the cable carries data rather than only power, and that the phone supports OTG. | .

589.title: TCP/IP (Network)
589.content: Some Meshtastic nodes support Wi-Fi/Ethernet connectivity, allowing TCP-based connections over your local network. Get the node onto your network first. Connect to it over Bluetooth or USB, open Settings → Device configuration → Network, and under Wi-Fi Options turn on WiFi Enabled and enter the SSID and Password. The Network screen appears only for nodes whose hardware supports Wi-Fi or Ethernet. Once the node has an address, come back and connect to it over the network. Connecting over the Network . | Make sure the node is on the same local network as your phone or desktop. | On the Connect tab, select Network in the transport selector. | Choose the node one of two ways: . | Scan for network devices: toggle this on to auto-discover nodes that advertise themselves on the local network (mDNS / _meshtastic._tcp). Discovered devices appear in the list; tap one to connect. | Add device manually…: enter the node’s IP address (or hostname) and port (default: 4403). | . | Previously used network addresses are remembered under Recent Network Devices for reconnection (touch & hold to remove one). | . Network discovery uses mDNS, which only works when both your phone and the node are on the same subnet. If the phone is not on Wi-Fi at all, the app warns that a network scan may find nothing. On Android 17 and newer, the app needs the Local network permission to reach a node on your own Wi-Fi at all, not only to discover it, so typing the address by hand does not work around a denied permission. Grant it from the card on the Network pane, or from the Permissions section of Settings. A node on a public address, or one reached over a VPN, needs no permission. When to Use TCP . | Node is on the same local network | Testing with a simulated node | Environments where Bluetooth has interference issues | . WLAN Unterstützung für mPWRD-OS . Settings → Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS is a separate, narrower tool. It sends Wi-Fi credentials over Bluetooth to mPWRD-OS devices only, using their own protocol. It does not configure Wi-Fi on an ordinary Meshtastic node. It is available on both Android and desktop. | Open the screen and wait while the app finds the device over Bluetooth. | Tap Scan for Networks, then pick a network from Available Networks, or turn on Hidden network and type the name into Network Name (SSID). | Enter the Password and tap Apply. | . If the scan reports No networks found or fails outright, move the phone closer to the device and scan again. If Failed to apply Wi-Fi configuration comes back, check the password and try again.

590.title: After Your First Connection
590.content: Being connected is not the same as being able to transmit. A node leaves the factory with no LoRa region set, and it does not transmit until you set one. When you connect such a node, the Connect tab shows a Set your region card; tap it to open the LoRa screen and choose the region you are in. Once the region is set, the tab warns you if the node is receive-only: a Transmit is disabled card, reading “This device can receive but will not send anything over LoRa.” Tap it to open the same screen and turn Transmit Enabled back on. Only one of the two cards appears at a time. An unset region already stops the node transmitting, so the app names that first and holds the transmit card back until you have set a region. For more information, see Settings — Radio & User.

591.title: Live Update
591.content: On Android 16 and newer, the Connect tab has a Live Update row while you are connected. It puts one thing you choose in the status bar and the service notification: . | Mesh status: the connection, how many nodes are online, your unread messages and your node’s battery. The status bar shows the nodes online, such as 5/12. | Track a node: one node’s battery, signal, when it was last heard, its hops and its distance from your node. The status bar shows its battery, or how long ago it was heard when it reports no battery. Pick the node from a list with favorites first, then the most recently heard, or search it by name. | . Tap the row to start one, switch to the other, or stop it. Only one runs at a time, and it is off until you start it. On a node’s details, Track in Live Update starts tracking that node directly. A dropped link keeps it running and shows the connection state until the node is back. Disconnecting, switching nodes, or deleting or ignoring the tracked node stops it. If the row says Live Updates are turned off for Meshtastic, Android shows it as an ordinary notification until you allow them in system settings.

592.title: Reconnection Behavior
592.content: The app reconnects to the last selected node on startup. You can switch transports from the Connect tab at any time. To disconnect, tap the disconnect button on the Connect tab: .

593.title: Quick Settings Tile
593.content: On Android you can add a Meshtastic tile to Quick Settings: pull down the notification shade, tap the edit (pencil) button, and drag the tile into place. | Connected - the tile is on and shows your node’s short name. Tap it to disconnect, the same as the disconnect button on the Connect tab. | Connecting - the tile is on and reads “Connecting”. Tap it to cancel. | Disconnected or Device sleeping - the tile is off. Tap it to reconnect to the node you last selected. | No device selected - tap the tile to open the Connect tab and pick a node. | . Disconnecting forgets the selected node, so after a disconnect the tile opens the Connect tab. If Android does not let the app reconnect in the background, the tile opens the app instead and the connection starts from there. On a locked phone the tile asks you to unlock first.

594.title: Desktop Connections
594.content: On Desktop (Linux/macOS/Windows), the app supports: . | Bluetooth (BLE) — via the Kable library; works on macOS, Linux, and Windows | USB Serial — primary wired connection method | TCP/IP — for network-connected nodes | . See Desktop App for platform-specific details and keyboard shortcuts.

596.title: Contributing
596.content: Guidelines for contributing to the Meshtastic Android/Desktop project (a KMP codebase that also compiles for iOS).

597.title: Branch Naming
597.content: Branches use conventional-commit style prefixes: . | Prefix | Use for | . | feat/<scope> | New user-visible behavior | . | fix/<scope> | Bug fixes | . | refactor/<scope> | Code structure changes | . | chore/<scope> | Tooling, deps, CI, cleanup | . | docs/<scope> | Documentation only | . | build/<scope> | Build system changes | . | ci/<scope> | CI workflow changes | . | test/<scope> | Test additions or fixes | . | deps/<scope> | Dependency updates | . Spec-driven work takes no prefix from that list: a numeric spec prefix (005-tak-v2-protocol) or the timestamp form YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-feature-name created by /speckit.git.feature. release/* and automation/* are reserved for maintainers and automated workflows. Examples: . | feat/desktop-ble-transport | fix/bluetooth-reconnect | 20260601-074653-air-quality-telemetry | .

598.title: Development Workflow
598.content: . | Fork the repository (external contributors) or create a branch (maintainers). | Implement your changes following the architecture guidelines. | Test locally: ./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt detektTypeResolved assembleDebug kmpSmokeCompile test allTests | Commit with clear, descriptive messages. | Push and open a Pull Request. | .

599.title: Commit Messages
599.content: Follow conventional commit style: . feat(docs): add in-app documentation browser fix(ble): handle reconnection timeout refactor(navigation): migrate to typed routes test(search): add keyword ranking tests .

600.title: Pull Request Checklist
600.content: Before submitting: . | Code compiles on all targets: ./gradlew assembleDebug kmpSmokeCompile | All tests pass: ./gradlew test allTests | Code style passes: ./gradlew spotlessCheck | Static analysis passes: ./gradlew detekt detektTypeResolved | New code has appropriate test coverage | No android.* imports in commonMain | Koin modules registered if new DI is added | Routes added to Routes.kt and registered in NavigationConfig.kt if new navigation is introduced | Documentation updated if user-facing behavior changes | .

601.title: Code Style
601.content: . | Formatting: Enforced by Spotless, which runs ktfmt (kotlinlang style) and then ktlint, and checks only files changed since origin/main | Static analysis: Detekt with project-specific configuration (config/detekt/detekt.yml) | Imports: No wildcard imports; organized automatically by Spotless | Line length: 120 characters maximum | . Run formatting: ./gradlew spotlessApply .

602.title: Architecture Rules
602.content: . | Feature modules must not depend on other feature modules; feature:map-maplibre and feature:coverage building on feature:map and feature:map-terrain are the exceptions | commonMain must not contain android.*, java.io.*, or platform-specific imports | Prefer interface + DI over expect/actual for complex platform behaviors | All navigation routes must be @Serializable and defined in Routes.kt | Use Koin annotations (@Single, @Factory, @Module) for dependency injection | .

603.title: Verification
603.content: Full pre-merge verification: ./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt detektTypeResolved assembleDebug kmpSmokeCompile test allTests . CI compiles the test shards with -PwarningsAsErrors=true; add it locally to catch a new Kotlin warning before CI does. For docs-specific changes, also run the Gradle bundle checks and the scripts the docs-quality.yml workflow runs on every docs pull request: ./gradlew generateDocsBundle validateDocsBundle node scripts/validate-doc-links.js docs/en node scripts/check-doc-coverage.js . node scripts/check-doc-aliases.js . node scripts/check-doc-freshness.js docs/en --max-age-days=180 python3 scripts/docs/sync-locale-front-matter.py --check . Prose in docs/en/ follows Section 11 of the Meshtastic Client Design Standards — see Documentation Style for what’s specific to this repository.
