This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | Off | . | Çevre metrikleri modülü etkin | Report the attached environment sensors | Off | . | Environment Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Güç metrikleri modülü etkin | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | Off | . | Power Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Güç metrikleri ekran üzerinde etkin | Also show power readings on the device’s display | Off | . | Çevre metrikleri ekran üzerinde etkin | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | Off | . See Telemetry & Sensors for supported sensors and configuration recommendations. Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). Define a list of quick-send messages that can be transmitted without a phone connected — ideal for field use. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | Yok | . | Mesajlar | Newline-separated list of messages | Boş | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | Rotary Encoder | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | Off | . | Zil gönder | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | Off | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | Off | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . Codec2 audio support for low-bandwidth voice communication over the mesh. This is an experimental feature that encodes voice into very small data packets using the Codec2 codec. It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | CODEC2 örnekleme hızı | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | Varsayılan | . | CODEC 2 etkinleştirildi | Turn the audio module on | Off | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | PTT pini | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . GPIO control over the mesh network. Allows a remote node to read or write GPIO pins on another node — useful for activating relays, reading switches, or controlling external hardware from a distance. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Tanımlanmamış pin erişimine izin ver | Allow access to any GPIO pin (security risk) | Off | . | Mevcut pinler | Up to 4 GPIO pins this node exposes for remote read/write | Yok | . | Uzak Donanım etkin | Turn remote GPIO access on | Off | . Neighbor Info module . Broadcasts information about directly heard neighbors, enabling mesh topology mapping. Each enabled node periodically shares a list of the other nodes it can hear and their signal quality. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Komşu Bilgisi etkin | Turn neighbor broadcasting on | Off | . | LoRa üzerinden ilet | Also broadcast neighbor info over LoRa, not just MQTT and the connected app. Unavailable on a channel using the default key and name | Off | . | Update Interval | How often to broadcast the neighbor list, in seconds. Minimum 4 hours | 0 (firmware default) | . See Local Mesh Discovery for how to use neighbor data for mesh topology exploration. Ambient Lighting module . Controls onboard NeoPixel or other addressable RGB LEDs on supported hardware. Can be used for visual status indicators, notification lights, or decorative effects. Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Akım | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LED durumu | Turn the LED on or off | Off | . | Red / Green / Blue | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . Turns your node into a motion or door sensor alert system. When a GPIO pin detects a state change (motion detected, door opened), the node broadcasts an alert message over the mesh. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Algılama Sensörü etkinleştirildi | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | Off | . | İzlenecek GPIO pini | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | Minimum time between alert broadcasts | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | Arkadaşça isim | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Boş | . | Zil gönder | Include a bell character in alerts | Off | . | State Broadcast Interval | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | Ayarlanmamış | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | High | . | Use Internal Pull-up | Enable the pin’s internal pull-up resistor | Off | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. Counts nearby devices by passively listening for probe requests that phones and laptops emit when scanning for networks. Available only on ESP32 devices. Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | Pax sayacı etkin | Turn people counting on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must both be off on the node for it to work | Off | . | Update Interval | How often to report counts | — | . | WiFi Threshold (dBm) | Ignore Wi-Fi probes weaker than this, so distant devices aren’t counted | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . Status Message module . The status message has no module screen. It is edited with the rest of the node’s identity, on Settings — Radio & User. Mesh Beacon module . Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. TAK module . Team Awareness Kit integration for interoperability with ATAK and WinTAK. The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. See TAK Integration for detailed setup and usage.

4717.title: Yönetim
4717.content: Uzaktan Yönetim . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | Modify configuration. | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | Action | What it does | . | Set time | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | Yeniden başlat | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Kapat | Powers the node down | . | Fabrika ayarları | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | NodeDB sıfırla | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. Yedekleme & Geri yükleme . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. Gelişmiş . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. Clean Node Database . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. Hata Ayıklama Paneli . Opens the Packets and App logs tabs for viewing, filtering, and exporting diagnostic output. See Debug Logs for the full walkthrough. App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. Hakkında . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. Acknowledgements . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Troubleshooting remote admin . | “Could not reach node — try again or move closer.” The target may be out of range or offline, or it doesn’t list your node’s public key as an admin key. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. Reconnect it from the Connections screen. | Changes not applying — some settings require a reboot to take effect. Try the Reboot action after saving. | .

4720.doc: 設定：モジュールと管理
4720.title: 設定：モジュールと管理
4720.content: オプションの機能モジュールを設定し、デバイスの管理を行います。モジュールは、専用の機能で Meshtastic を拡張します。それぞれ個別に有効・無効を切り替えられます。 . Enable only the modules you use. 使わないモジュールを無効にすると、電波利用時間が減り、バッテリーを節約でき、設定もシンプルになります。 A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. モジュールの設定は、トグルスイッチ、ドロップダウン、テキストフィールド、スライダーを備えたカード形式のレイアウトを使用します： . .

4721.doc: 設定：モジュールと管理
4721.title: 追加機能の設定
4721.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification and Mesh Beacon are the exceptions: their button reads Save. External Notification may still restart the node for some changes, while a Mesh Beacon change applies without a restart. MQTT module . インターネット接続のために、メッシュのメッセージを MQTT サーバーとの間で橋渡しします。 This is how you extend your mesh beyond LoRa range or integrate with home automation systems. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | アドレス | MQTT サーバーのアドレス | mqtt.meshtastic.org | . | 暗号化の有効化 | Publish packets still encrypted with the channel key | On | . | JSON出力の有効化 | Publish and consume MQTT messages as JSON. Shown only for a node on firmware older than 2.8, which removed JSON support, or while the setting is still on | オフ | . | マップ報告 | Publish position to the public map — see the map reporting card that follows | オフ | . | クライアントへのプロキシの有効化 | Let the connected app carry the node’s MQTT traffic, instead of the node reaching the broker itself | オフ | . | MQTTを有効化 | Turn the MQTT bridge on | オフ | . | MQTT proxy in this app | The app-side half of MQTT Client Proxy: whether this app acts as that relay. It shows whether the relay is running, and can be turned on only while MQTT Enabled and MQTT Client Proxy are both on. See MQTT | — | . | パスワード | 認証用のパスワード | The public broker’s | . | ルート トピック | MQTT のベーストピックパス | msh | . | TLS Enabled | Use a secure connection | オフ | . | ユーザー名 | 認証用のユーザー名 | The public broker’s | . Turning Map Reporting on reveals a consent card headed Consent to Share Unencrypted Node Data via MQTT, with an I agree. switch under it. The rest of the card doesn’t exist on screen until you agree: . | 設定項目 | 説明 | . | 同意します。 | Explicit consent to transmit your node data, including an approximate position, unencrypted. Map reporting doesn’t start without it | . | Map Publish Interval | How often to report. A dropdown of fixed intervals from 1 hour to 72 hours — nothing shorter is offered | . | Precision slider | The slider has no label of its own. It sets how coarsely your position is published, from 12 to 15; the line beneath reads ± the resulting distance, in your own units | . 暗号化、プライバシー、サーバーの設定を含む詳しい使い方は、MQTT を参照してください。 . Serial module . 外部デバイスとの連携（GPS モジュール、センサー、カスタムハードウェア）のために、シリアルポート通信を有効にします。有効にすると、ノードのシリアルポートで protobuf またはテキストデータを送受信でき、外部のマイコンやコンピューターがメッシュとやり取りできるようになります。 . | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | シリアルボーレイト | Port speed, from 110 Baud to 921600 Baud | デフォルト | . | Echoを有効化 | Echo packets you send back over the serial port | オフ | . | シリアルモード | Which protocol the port speaks: Default, Simple, Protobufs, Text Message, NMEA Positions, or CalTopo, plus WS85, VE_DIRECT, MS_CONFIG, LOG and LOGTEXT under their firmware names | デフォルト | . | コンソールのシリアルポートを上書き | Take over the port the debug console normally uses | オフ | . | Receive data (rxd) GPIO pin / Transmit data (txd) GPIO pin | GPIO pins for the serial connection | 0 | . | シリアル通信を有効化 | Turn serial communication on | オフ | . | タイムアウト | How long to wait before treating received data as a complete packet. 0 uses 250 ms | 0 | . External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. メッセージ到着時に物理的に知らせる必要があるデバイスに便利です。特に無人設置や屋外設置で役立ちます。 . There are two independent triggers — an incoming message, and a received bell character — and each can drive the LED, the buzzer and the vibration motor separately, giving six toggles. The firmware turns the module on, and picks the outputs, on hardware that has a buzzer, vibration motor or notification LED; elsewhere everything starts off. | 設定項目 | 説明 | . | LED出力 アクティブハイ | Whether the LED pin is active high or low. Shown once Output pin GPIO is set | . | Alert when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell | Which outputs fire on a received bell character | . | Alert when receiving a message / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message / Vibra Motor Alert | Which outputs fire on an incoming message | . | 外部通知を有効化 | Master toggle for the module | . | GPIO Output Duration | How long a single alert lasts | . | Nag Timeout | Keep repeating the alert for this long until it is acknowledged. Unset disables nagging | . | LED出力 (GPIO) | Pin the LED is wired to | . | ブザー出力(GPIO) | Pin the buzzer is wired to | . | バイブレーション出力 (GPIO) | Pin the vibration motor is wired to | . | 着信音 | The tone played on a PWM buzzer, in RTTTL. Can be imported from a file | . | I2Sをブザーとして使用 | Send the alert through an I2S audio output instead | . | PWMブザーを使用 | Drive the buzzer with PWM, which allows tones rather than a single pitch. Shown once Output pin buzzer GPIO is set | . Store & Forward module . 一時的にオフラインだったノードのためにメッセージをバッファリングし、それらのノードが再接続したときに再送します。ノードが頻繁に圏内・圏外を行き来するメッシュに不可欠です。短時間の切断中にメッセージが失われないようにします。 A server needs an ESP32 with PSRAM or a Linux meshtasticd node. A node in the Router or Router Late role acts as a server even with the server setting off. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | リクエスト可能な最大の履歴件数 | Most stored messages returned per request. 0 uses 25 | 0 | . | リクエスト可能な履歴の期間 (分) | How far back, in minutes, stored messages are returned. 0 uses 240 | 0 | . | サーバーの最大保管レコード数 (デフォルト 約11,000レコード) | Most messages to store. 0 uses three quarters of the free PSRAM | 0 | . | ハートビート | Periodically announce that this node is a store-and-forward server | オフ | . | サーバー | Act as a store-and-forward server for the mesh | オフ | . | ストアアンドフォワード有効 | Turn store and forward on | オフ | . Range Test module . ノード間のリンク品質を評価するための、自動レンジテストツールです。有効にすると、ノードはカウンターを増やしながらテストメッセージを定期的に送信します。受信側のノードがこれらのメッセージを記録するため、歩いたり車で移動したりして、後からどの距離でメッセージが届かなくなったかを分析できます。 . Range Test only works on a secured primary channel. As long as your primary channel still uses the default channel key, the interval and CSV controls stay disabled — you can still switch an already-enabled module off — and saving force-disables the module if the channel has reverted to public. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | レンジテストを有効化 | Turn range testing on | オフ | . | ストレージにCSVファイルを保存(ESP32のみ) | Log received test data as a CSV on the node’s own filesystem. ESP32 nodes only | オフ | . | Sender Interval | Time between test transmissions, chosen from a dropdown of fixed intervals. Unset stops sending | 未設定 | . Telemetry module . ノードがメッシュと共有するテレメトリデータを制御します。テレメトリには、デバイスの状態（バッテリー、連続稼働時間）と環境センサーのデータ（温度、湿度、気圧）が含まれます。 . Each of the four metric groups has its own enable toggle and its own interval, so you can report battery health often and sensors rarely. The intervals run from 30 minutes to 72 hours. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | 空気品質測定モジュールを有効化 | Report particulate and CO₂ sensor data | オフ | . | 空気品質メトリクスの更新間隔 | How often to report them | — | . | デバイステレメトリを送信 | Send device metrics to the mesh. When it is off, they go only to connected clients. Only shown on firmware 2.7.13 and newer | オフ | . | デバイスメトリクスの更新間隔 | How often to report battery, uptime and channel utilization | — | . | 環境メトリクスは華氏を使用 | Use °F on the device’s display. This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | オフ | . | 環境メトリクスモジュールを有効化 | Report the attached environment sensors | オフ | . | 環境メトリクスの更新間隔 | How often to report them | — | . | 電源メトリクスモジュール有効 | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | オフ | . | 電源メトリクスの更新間隔 | How often to report them | — | . | 電源メトリクスを画面上で有効化 | Also show power readings on the device’s display | オフ | . | 環境メトリクスを画面上で有効化 | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | オフ | . 対応センサーと設定の推奨事項については、テレメトリとセンサー を参照してください。 . Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). スマートフォンを接続していなくても送信できる、クイック送信メッセージのリストを定義します。フィールドでの使用に最適です。 . | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | なし | . | メッセージ | 改行で区切ったメッセージのリスト | Empty | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | ロータリーエンコーダー | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | オフ | . | アラートメッセージ付きのベルを送信 | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | オフ | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | オフ | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . メッシュ上での低帯域幅の音声通信のための、Codec2 音声サポートです。これは、Codec2 コーデックを使って音声を非常に小さなデータパケットにエンコードする、実験的な機能です。 It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | CODEC2 サンプルレート | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | デフォルト | . | CODEC 2 を有効化 | Turn the audio module on | オフ | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | PTT端子 | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . メッシュネットワーク経由での GPIO 制御です。リモートのノードが、別のノードの GPIO ピンを読み書きできるようにします。リレーの作動、スイッチの読み取り、離れた場所からの外部ハードウェア制御に便利です。 . ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | 未定義のピンへのアクセスを許可 | 任意の GPIO ピンへのアクセスを許可（セキュリティリスク） | オフ | . | 使用可能な端子 | このノードがリモートの読み書き用に公開する GPIO ピン（最大 4 個） | なし | . | リモートハードウェアを有効化 | Turn remote GPIO access on | オフ | . Neighbor Info module . 直接受信した隣接ノードの情報をブロードキャストし、メッシュのトポロジーマッピングを可能にします。有効にした各ノードは、受信できる他のノードとその信号品質のリストを定期的に共有します。 . | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | 近隣ノード情報を有効化 | Turn neighbor broadcasting on | オフ | . | LoRaで送信 | Also broadcast neighbor info over LoRa, not just MQTT and the connected app. デフォルトの鍵と名前を使用しているチャンネルでは利用できません | オフ | . | GPS ポーリング間隔 | How often to broadcast the neighbor list, in seconds. Minimum 4 hours | 0 (firmware default) | . See Local Mesh Discovery for how to use neighbor data for mesh topology exploration. Ambient Lighting module . 対応ハードウェア上の、オンボードの NeoPixel やその他のアドレサブル RGB LED を制御します。視覚的なステータス表示、通知ライト、装飾的な演出に使用できます。 . Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | 電流 | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LEDの状態 | LED のオン／オフを切り替え | オフ | . | 赤／緑／青 | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . ノードを、動きやドアを検知するセンサーアラートシステムに変えます。 GPIO ピンが状態の変化（動きの検知、ドアの開放）を検出すると、ノードはメッシュ経由でアラートメッセージをブロードキャストします。 . | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | 検出センサーを有効化 | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | オフ | . | モニターのGPIOピン | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | アラートのブロードキャスト間の最小時間 | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | 名前 | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Empty | . | アラートメッセージ付きのベルを送信 | Include a bell character in alerts | オフ | . | State Broadcast Interval | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | 未設定 | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | 高 | . | Use Internal Pull-up | ピンの内蔵プルアップ抵抗を有効にする | オフ | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. スマートフォンやノートパソコンがネットワークを探すときに発するプローブ要求を受動的に受信して、近くのデバイスを数えます。 ESP32 デバイスでのみ利用できます。 Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | 設定 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | Paxcounter を有効化 | Turn people counting on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must both be off on the node for it to work | オフ | . | GPS ポーリング間隔 | カウントを報告する頻度 | — | . | WiFi Threshold (dBm) | Ignore Wi-Fi probes weaker than this, so distant devices aren’t counted | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . Status Message module . The status message has no module screen. It is edited with the rest of the node’s identity, on Settings — Radio & User. Mesh Beacon module . Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. TAK module . ATAK および WinTAK と相互運用するための、Team Awareness Kit 連携です。 The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. 詳しい設定と使い方は、TAK 連携 を参照してください。 .

4722.doc: 設定：モジュールと管理
4722.title: 管理
4722.content: リモート管理 . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | 設定を変更します。 | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | 操作 | 内容 | . | 時刻を設定 | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | 再起動 | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | シャットダウン | Powers the node down | . | 出荷時にリセット | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | NodeDBをリセット | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. バックアップと復元 . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. 詳細設定 . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. ノードデータベースの整理 . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. デバッグ . 診断出力の表示・絞り込み・エクスポートを行う「パケット」タブと「アプリログ」タブを開きます。詳しい手順は、デバッグログ を参照してください。 . App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. 概要 . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. 謝辞 . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Troubleshooting remote admin . | “Could not reach node — try again or move closer.” The target may be out of range or offline, or it doesn’t list your node’s public key as an admin key. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. Reconnect it from the Connections screen. | 変更が適用されない：一部の設定は、反映に再起動が必要です。保存後に「再起動」を実行してみてください。 | .

4724.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4724.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4725.title: Module configuration
4725.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification and Mesh Beacon are the exceptions: their button reads Save. External Notification may still restart the node for some changes, while a Mesh Beacon change applies without a restart. MQTT module . Bridges mesh messages to and from an MQTT broker for internet connectivity. This is how you extend your mesh beyond LoRa range or integrate with home automation systems. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Address | MQTT broker address | mqtt.meshtastic.org | . | Encryption Enabled | Publish packets still encrypted with the channel key | On | . | JSON output enabled | Publish and consume MQTT messages as JSON. Shown only for a node on firmware older than 2.8, which removed JSON support, or while the setting is still on | Off | . | Map Reporting | Publish position to the public map — see the map reporting card that follows | Off | . | MQTT Client Proxy | Let the connected app carry the node’s MQTT traffic, instead of the node reaching the broker itself | Off | . | MQTT Enabled | Turn the MQTT bridge on | Off | . | MQTT proxy in this app | The app-side half of MQTT Client Proxy: whether this app acts as that relay. It shows whether the relay is running, and can be turned on only while MQTT Enabled and MQTT Client Proxy are both on. See MQTT | — | . | Password | Authentication password | The public broker’s | . | Root Topic | Base MQTT topic path | msh | . | TLS Enabled | Use a secure connection | Off | . | Username | Authentication username | The public broker’s | . Turning Map Reporting on reveals a consent card headed Consent to Share Unencrypted Node Data via MQTT, with an I agree. switch under it. The rest of the card doesn’t exist on screen until you agree: . | Setting | Description | . | I agree. | Explicit consent to transmit your node data, including an approximate position, unencrypted. Map reporting doesn’t start without it | . | Map Publish Interval | How often to report. A dropdown of fixed intervals from 1 hour to 72 hours — nothing shorter is offered | . | Precision slider | The slider has no label of its own. It sets how coarsely your position is published, from 12 to 15; the line beneath reads ± the resulting distance, in your own units | . See MQTT for a detailed usage guide including encryption, privacy, and broker setup. Serial module . Enables serial port communication for external device integrations (GPS modules, sensors, or custom hardware). When enabled, the node’s serial port can send and receive protobuf or text data, allowing external microcontrollers or computers to interact with the mesh. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Baud | Port speed, from 110 Baud to 921600 Baud | Default | . | Echo | Echo packets you send back over the serial port | Off | . | Mode | Which protocol the port speaks: Default, Simple, Protobufs, Text Message, NMEA Positions, or CalTopo, plus WS85, VE_DIRECT, MS_CONFIG, LOG and LOGTEXT under their firmware names | Default | . | Override console serial port | Take over the port the debug console normally uses | Off | . | Receive data (rxd) GPIO pin / Transmit data (txd) GPIO pin | GPIO pins for the serial connection | 0 | . | Serial Enabled | Turn serial communication on | Off | . | Timeout | How long to wait before treating received data as a complete packet. 0 uses 250 ms | 0 | . External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. Useful for devices that need to physically signal when a message arrives — particularly helpful for unattended or outdoor installations. There are two independent triggers — an incoming message, and a received bell character — and each can drive the LED, the buzzer and the vibration motor separately, giving six toggles. The firmware turns the module on, and picks the outputs, on hardware that has a buzzer, vibration motor or notification LED; elsewhere everything starts off. | Setting | Description | . | Active | Whether the LED pin is active high or low. Shown once Output pin GPIO is set | . | Alert when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell | Which outputs fire on a received bell character | . | Alert when receiving a message / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message / Vibra Motor Alert | Which outputs fire on an incoming message | . | External Notification Enabled | Master toggle for the module | . | GPIO Output Duration | How long a single alert lasts | . | Nag Timeout | Keep repeating the alert for this long until it is acknowledged. Unset disables nagging | . | Output pin GPIO | Pin the LED is wired to | . | Output pin buzzer GPIO | Pin the buzzer is wired to | . | Output pin vibra GPIO | Pin the vibration motor is wired to | . | Ringtone | The tone played on a PWM buzzer, in RTTTL. Can be imported from a file | . | Use I2S As Buzzer | Send the alert through an I2S audio output instead | . | Use PWM Buzzer | Drive the buzzer with PWM, which allows tones rather than a single pitch. Shown once Output pin buzzer GPIO is set | . Store & Forward module . Buffers messages for nodes that were temporarily offline, then replays them when those nodes reconnect. Essential for meshes where nodes go in and out of range regularly — ensures messages aren’t lost during brief disconnections. A server needs an ESP32 with PSRAM or a Linux meshtasticd node. A node in the Router or Router Late role acts as a server even with the server setting off. | Setting | Description | Default | . | History Return Max | Most stored messages returned per request. 0 uses 25 | 0 | . | History Return Window | How far back, in minutes, stored messages are returned. 0 uses 240 | 0 | . | Number of records | Most messages to store. 0 uses three quarters of the free PSRAM | 0 | . | Send Heartbeat | Periodically announce that this node is a store-and-forward server | Off | . | Server | Act as a store-and-forward server for the mesh | Off | . | Store and Forward Enabled | Turn store and forward on | Off | . Range Test module . Automated range testing tool for evaluating link quality between nodes. When enabled, the node periodically transmits test messages with incrementing counters. A receiver node logs these messages, allowing you to walk or drive away and later analyze at what distance messages stopped arriving. Range Test only works on a secured primary channel. As long as your primary channel still uses the default channel key, the interval and CSV controls stay disabled — you can still switch an already-enabled module off — and saving force-disables the module if the channel has reverted to public. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Range Test Enabled | Turn range testing on | Off | . | Save | Log received test data as a CSV on the node’s own filesystem. ESP32 nodes only | Off | . | Sender Interval | Time between test transmissions, chosen from a dropdown of fixed intervals. Unset stops sending | Unset | . Telemetry module . Controls what telemetry data your node shares with the mesh. Telemetry includes device health (battery, uptime) and environmental sensor data (temperature, humidity, pressure). Each of the four metric groups has its own enable toggle and its own interval, so you can report battery health often and sensors rarely. The intervals run from 30 minutes to 72 hours. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Air Quality Metrics Enabled | Report particulate and CO₂ sensor data | Off | . | Air Quality Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Broadcast Device Metrics | Send device metrics to the mesh. When it is off, they go only to connected clients. Only shown on firmware 2.7.13 and newer | Off | . | Device Metrics Interval | How often to report battery, uptime and channel utilization | — | . | Display Fahrenheit | Use °F on the device’s display. This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | Off | . | Environment Metrics Enabled | Report the attached environment sensors | Off | . | Environment Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Power Measurement Enabled | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | Off | . | Power Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Power Screen | Also show power readings on the device’s display | Off | . | Show on device screen | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | Off | . See Telemetry & Sensors for supported sensors and configuration recommendations. Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). Define a list of quick-send messages that can be transmitted without a phone connected — ideal for field use. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | None | . | Messages | Newline-separated list of messages | Empty | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | Rotary Encoder | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | Off | . | Send Bell | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | Off | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | Off | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . Codec2 audio support for low-bandwidth voice communication over the mesh. This is an experimental feature that encodes voice into very small data packets using the Codec2 codec. It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Bitrate | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | Default | . | Codec2 Enabled | Turn the audio module on | Off | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | PTT Pin | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . GPIO control over the mesh network. Allows a remote node to read or write GPIO pins on another node — useful for activating relays, reading switches, or controlling external hardware from a distance. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Allow undefined pin access | Allow access to any GPIO pin (security risk) | Off | . | Available pins | Up to 4 GPIO pins this node exposes for remote read/write | None | . | Remote Hardware enabled | Turn remote GPIO access on | Off | . Neighbor Info module . Broadcasts information about directly heard neighbors, enabling mesh topology mapping. Each enabled node periodically shares a list of the other nodes it can hear and their signal quality. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Neighbor Info Enabled | Turn neighbor broadcasting on | Off | . | Transmit over LoRa | Also broadcast neighbor info over LoRa, not just MQTT and the connected app. Unavailable on a channel using the default key and name | Off | . | Update Interval | How often to broadcast the neighbor list, in seconds. Minimum 4 hours | 0 (firmware default) | . See Local Mesh Discovery for how to use neighbor data for mesh topology exploration. Ambient Lighting module . Controls onboard NeoPixel or other addressable RGB LEDs on supported hardware. Can be used for visual status indicators, notification lights, or decorative effects. Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Current | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LED State | Turn the LED on or off | Off | . | Red / Green / Blue | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . Turns your node into a motion or door sensor alert system. When a GPIO pin detects a state change (motion detected, door opened), the node broadcasts an alert message over the mesh. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Detection Sensor Enabled | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | Off | . | GPIO Pin to monitor | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | Minimum time between alert broadcasts | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | Name | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Empty | . | Send Bell | Include a bell character in alerts | Off | . | State Broadcast Interval | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | Unset | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | High | . | Use Internal Pull-up | Enable the pin’s internal pull-up resistor | Off | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. Counts nearby devices by passively listening for probe requests that phones and laptops emit when scanning for networks. Available only on ESP32 devices. Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | Setting | Description | Default | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | PAX Counter Enabled | Turn people counting on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must both be off on the node for it to work | Off | . | Update Interval | How often to report counts | — | . | WiFi Threshold (dBm) | Ignore Wi-Fi probes weaker than this, so distant devices aren’t counted | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . Status Message module . The status message has no module screen. It is edited with the rest of the node’s identity, on Settings — Radio & User. Mesh Beacon module . Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. TAK module . Team Awareness Kit integration for interoperability with ATAK and WinTAK. The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. See TAK Integration for detailed setup and usage.

4729.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4729.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4730.title: 모듈 설정
4730.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification and Mesh Beacon are the exceptions: their button reads Save. External Notification may still restart the node for some changes, while a Mesh Beacon change applies without a restart. MQTT module . Bridges mesh messages to and from an MQTT broker for internet connectivity. This is how you extend your mesh beyond LoRa range or integrate with home automation systems. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 서버 주소 | MQTT broker address | mqtt.meshtastic.org | . | 암호화 사용 | Publish packets still encrypted with the channel key | On | . | JSON 사용 | Publish and consume MQTT messages as JSON. Shown only for a node on firmware older than 2.8, which removed JSON support, or while the setting is still on | Off | . | Map Reporting | Publish position to the public map — see the map reporting card that follows | Off | . | Proxy to client 사용 | Let the connected app carry the node’s MQTT traffic, instead of the node reaching the broker itself | Off | . | MQTT 활성화 | Turn the MQTT bridge on | Off | . | MQTT proxy in this app | The app-side half of MQTT Client Proxy: whether this app acts as that relay. It shows whether the relay is running, and can be turned on only while MQTT Enabled and MQTT Client Proxy are both on. See MQTT | — | . | 비밀번호 | Authentication password | The public broker’s | . | Root topic | Base MQTT topic path | msh | . | TLS Enabled | Use a secure connection | Off | . | 사용자명 | Authentication username | The public broker’s | . Turning Map Reporting on reveals a consent card headed Consent to Share Unencrypted Node Data via MQTT, with an I agree. switch under it. The rest of the card doesn’t exist on screen until you agree: . | Setting | 설명 | . | 동의합니다. | Explicit consent to transmit your node data, including an approximate position, unencrypted. Map reporting doesn’t start without it | . | Map Publish Interval | How often to report. A dropdown of fixed intervals from 1 hour to 72 hours — nothing shorter is offered | . | Precision slider | The slider has no label of its own. It sets how coarsely your position is published, from 12 to 15; the line beneath reads ± the resulting distance, in your own units | . See MQTT for a detailed usage guide including encryption, privacy, and broker setup. Serial module . Enables serial port communication for external device integrations (GPS modules, sensors, or custom hardware). When enabled, the node’s serial port can send and receive protobuf or text data, allowing external microcontrollers or computers to interact with the mesh. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 시리얼 baud rate | Port speed, from 110 Baud to 921600 Baud | 기본값 | . | 에코 활성화 | Echo packets you send back over the serial port | Off | . | 시리얼 모드 | Which protocol the port speaks: Default, Simple, Protobufs, Text Message, NMEA Positions, or CalTopo, plus WS85, VE_DIRECT, MS_CONFIG, LOG and LOGTEXT under their firmware names | 기본값 | . | Override console serial port | Take over the port the debug console normally uses | Off | . | Receive data (rxd) GPIO pin / Transmit data (txd) GPIO pin | GPIO pins for the serial connection | 0 | . | 시리얼 활성화 | Turn serial communication on | Off | . | 시간 초과 | How long to wait before treating received data as a complete packet. 0 uses 250 ms | 0 | . External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. Useful for devices that need to physically signal when a message arrives — particularly helpful for unattended or outdoor installations. There are two independent triggers — an incoming message, and a received bell character — and each can drive the LED, the buzzer and the vibration motor separately, giving six toggles. The firmware turns the module on, and picks the outputs, on hardware that has a buzzer, vibration motor or notification LED; elsewhere everything starts off. | Setting | 설명 | . | LED 출력 active high | Whether the LED pin is active high or low. Shown once Output pin GPIO is set | . | Alert when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell | Which outputs fire on a received bell character | . | Alert when receiving a message / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message / Vibra Motor Alert | Which outputs fire on an incoming message | . | 외부 알림 활성화 | Master toggle for the module | . | GPIO Output Duration | How long a single alert lasts | . | Nag Timeout | Keep repeating the alert for this long until it is acknowledged. Unset disables nagging | . | LED 출력 (GPIO) | Pin the LED is wired to | . | 부저 출력 (GPIO) | Pin the buzzer is wired to | . | 진동 출력 (GPIO) | Pin the vibration motor is wired to | . | 벨소리 | The tone played on a PWM buzzer, in RTTTL. Can be imported from a file | . | I2S 부저 사용 | Send the alert through an I2S audio output instead | . | PWM 부저 사용 | Drive the buzzer with PWM, which allows tones rather than a single pitch. Shown once Output pin buzzer GPIO is set | . Store & Forward module . Buffers messages for nodes that were temporarily offline, then replays them when those nodes reconnect. Essential for meshes where nodes go in and out of range regularly — ensures messages aren’t lost during brief disconnections. A server needs an ESP32 with PSRAM or a Linux meshtasticd node. A node in the Router or Router Late role acts as a server even with the server setting off. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | History Return Max | Most stored messages returned per request. 0 uses 25 | 0 | . | History Return Window | How far back, in minutes, stored messages are returned. 0 uses 240 | 0 | . | Number of records | Most messages to store. 0 uses three quarters of the free PSRAM | 0 | . | Send Heartbeat | Periodically announce that this node is a store-and-forward server | Off | . | 서버 | Act as a store-and-forward server for the mesh | Off | . | Store and Forward Enabled | Turn store and forward on | Off | . A receiver node logs these messages, allowing you to walk or drive away and later analyze at what distance messages stopped arriving. Range Test only works on a secured primary channel. As long as your primary channel still uses the default channel key, the interval and CSV controls stay disabled — you can still switch an already-enabled module off — and saving force-disables the module if the channel has reverted to public. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 거리 테스트 활성화 | Turn range testing on | Off | . | .CSV 파일 저장 (EPS32만 동작) | Log received test data as a CSV on the node’s own filesystem. ESP32 nodes only | Off | . | Sender Interval | Time between test transmissions, chosen from a dropdown of fixed intervals. Unset stops sending | 해제 | . Telemetry module . Each of the four metric groups has its own enable toggle and its own interval, so you can report battery health often and sensors rarely. The intervals run from 30 minutes to 72 hours. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 대기질 메트릭 모듈 사용 | Report particulate and CO₂ sensor data | Off | . | Air Quality Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | Broadcast Device Metrics | Send device metrics to the mesh. When it is off, they go only to connected clients. Only shown on firmware 2.7.13 and newer | Off | . | Device Metrics Interval | How often to report battery, uptime and channel utilization | — | . | 환경 메트릭에서 화씨 사용 | Use °F on the device’s display. This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | Off | . | 환경 메트릭 모듈 사용 | Report the attached environment sensors | Off | . | Environment Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | 전력 메트릭 모듈 사용 | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | Off | . | Power Metrics Interval | How often to report them | — | . | 전력 메트릭 화면 사용 | Also show power readings on the device’s display | Off | . | 환경 메트릭 화면 사용 | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | Off | . See Telemetry & Sensors for supported sensors and configuration recommendations. Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). Define a list of quick-send messages that can be transmitted without a phone connected — ideal for field use. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | 없음 | . | 메시지기기 | Newline-separated list of messages | Empty | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | Rotary Encoder | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | Off | . | 벨 전송 | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | Off | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | Off | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | CODEC2 샘플 레이트 | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | 기본값 | . | CODEC2 활성화 | Turn the audio module on | Off | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | PTT 핀 | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . GPIO control over the mesh network. Allows a remote node to read or write GPIO pins on another node — useful for activating relays, reading switches, or controlling external hardware from a distance. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | Allow undefined pin access | Allow access to any GPIO pin (security risk) | Off | . | Available pins | Up to 4 GPIO pins this node exposes for remote read/write | 없음 | . | 원격 하드웨어 활성화 | Turn remote GPIO access on | Off | . Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 전류 | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LED 상태 | Turn the LED on or off | Off | . | Red / Green / Blue | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . Turns your node into a motion or door sensor alert system. When a GPIO pin detects a state change (motion detected, door opened), the node broadcasts an alert message over the mesh. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | 감지 센서 활성화 | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | Off | . | 상태 모니터링 GPIO 핀 | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | Minimum time between alert broadcasts | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | 식별 이름 | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Empty | . | 벨 전송 | Include a bell character in alerts | Off | . | State Broadcast Interval | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | 해제 | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | High | . | Use Internal Pull-up | Enable the pin’s internal pull-up resistor | Off | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. Counts nearby devices by passively listening for probe requests that phones and laptops emit when scanning for networks. Available only on ESP32 devices. Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | 팍스카운터 활성화 | Turn people counting on. TAK module . Team Awareness Kit integration for interoperability with ATAK and WinTAK. The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. 4736.title: Administración
4736.content: Administración remota . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | Modify configuration. | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | Action | What it does | . | Set time | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | Reiniciar | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Apagar | Powers the node down | . | Restablecer los valores de fábrica | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | Reinicio de NodeDB | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. Hacer copia de seguridad y restaurar . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. Avanzado . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. Limpiar nodos de la base de datos . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. Panel de depuración . Opens the Packets and App logs tabs for viewing, filtering, and exporting diagnostic output. See Debug Logs for the full walkthrough. App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. Acerca de . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. Agradecimientos . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Troubleshooting remote admin . | “Could not reach node — try again or move closer.” The target may be out of range or offline, or it doesn’t list your node’s public key as an admin key. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. Reconnect it from the Connections screen. | Changes not applying — some settings require a reboot to take effect. Try the Reboot action after saving. | .

4739.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4739.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4741.title: Διαχείριση
4741.content: Απομακρυσμένη Διαχείριση . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | Modify configuration. | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | Action | What it does | . | Set time | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | Επανεκκίνηση | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Τερματισμός λειτουργίας | Powers the node down | . | Επαναφορά εργοστασιακών ρυθμίσεων | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | NodeDB reset | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. Backup & Restore . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. Advanced . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. Clean Node Database . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. Πίνακας αποσφαλμάτωσης . Opens the Packets and App logs tabs for viewing, filtering, and exporting diagnostic output. See Debug Logs for the full walkthrough. App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. Σχετικά . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. Acknowledgements . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. 4744.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4744.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .
