4857.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4857.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4862.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4862.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4863.title: Modul beállítások
4863.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification and Mesh Beacon are the exceptions: their button reads Save. External Notification may still restart the node for some changes, while a Mesh Beacon change applies without a restart. MQTT module . Bridges mesh messages to and from an MQTT broker for internet connectivity. This is how you extend your mesh beyond LoRa range or integrate with home automation systems. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Cím | MQTT broker address | mqtt.meshtastic.org | . | Titkosítás engedélyezve | Publish packets still encrypted with the channel key | On | . | JSON kimenet engedélyezve | Publish and consume MQTT messages as JSON. Shown only for a node on firmware older than 2.8, which removed JSON support, or while the setting is still on | Off | . | Map Reporting | Publish position to the public map — see the map reporting card that follows | Off | . | Proxy kliens felé engedélyezve | Let the connected app carry the node’s MQTT traffic, instead of the node reaching the broker itself | Off | . | MQTT engedélyezve | Turn the MQTT bridge on | Off | . | MQTT proxy in this app | The app-side half of MQTT Client Proxy: whether this app acts as that relay. It shows whether the relay is running, and can be turned on only while MQTT Enabled and MQTT Client Proxy are both on. See MQTT | — | . | Jelszó | Authentication password | The public broker’s | . | Gyökér téma | Base MQTT topic path | msh | . | TLS Enabled | Use a secure connection | Off | . | Felhasználónév | Authentication username | The public broker’s | . Turning Map Reporting on reveals a consent card headed Consent to Share Unencrypted Node Data via MQTT, with an I agree. switch under it. The rest of the card doesn’t exist on screen until you agree: . | Setting | Leírás | . | Elfogadom. | Explicit consent to transmit your node data, including an approximate position, unencrypted. Map reporting doesn’t start without it | . | Map Publish Interval | How often to report. A dropdown of fixed intervals from 1 hour to 72 hours — nothing shorter is offered | . | Precision slider | The slider has no label of its own. It sets how coarsely your position is published, from 12 to 15; the line beneath reads ± the resulting distance, in your own units | . See MQTT for a detailed usage guide including encryption, privacy, and broker setup. Serial module . Enables serial port communication for external device integrations (GPS modules, sensors, or custom hardware). When enabled, the node’s serial port can send and receive protobuf or text data, allowing external microcontrollers or computers to interact with the mesh. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Soros baud ráta | Port speed, from 110 Baud to 921600 Baud | Alapértelmezett | . | Echo engedélyezve | Echo packets you send back over the serial port | Off | . | Soros mód | Which protocol the port speaks: Default, Simple, Protobufs, Text Message, NMEA Positions, or CalTopo, plus WS85, VE_DIRECT, MS_CONFIG, LOG and LOGTEXT under their firmware names | Alapértelmezett | . | Konzol soros port felülbírálása | Take over the port the debug console normally uses | Off | . | Receive data (rxd) GPIO pin / Transmit data (txd) GPIO pin | GPIO pins for the serial connection | 0 | . | Soros engedélyezve | Turn serial communication on | Off | . | Időtúllépés | How long to wait before treating received data as a complete packet. 0 uses 250 ms | 0 | . External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. Useful for devices that need to physically signal when a message arrives — particularly helpful for unattended or outdoor installations. There are two independent triggers — an incoming message, and a received bell character — and each can drive the LED, the buzzer and the vibration motor separately, giving six toggles. The firmware turns the module on, and picks the outputs, on hardware that has a buzzer, vibration motor or notification LED; elsewhere everything starts off. | Setting | Leírás | . | Kimeneti LED aktív magas szint | Whether the LED pin is active high or low. Shown once Output pin GPIO is set | . | Alert when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell | Which outputs fire on a received bell character | . | Alert when receiving a message / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message / Vibra Motor Alert | Which outputs fire on an incoming message | . | Külső értesítés engedélyezve | Master toggle for the module | . | GPIO Output Duration | How long a single alert lasts | . | Nag Timeout | Keep repeating the alert for this long until it is acknowledged. Unset disables nagging | . | Kimeneti LED (GPIO) | Pin the LED is wired to | . | Kimeneti csipogó (GPIO) | Pin the buzzer is wired to | . | Kimeneti rezgő (GPIO) | Pin the vibration motor is wired to | . | Csengőhang | The tone played on a PWM buzzer, in RTTTL. Can be imported from a file | . | I2S használata csipogóként | Send the alert through an I2S audio output instead | . | PWM csipogó használata | Drive the buzzer with PWM, which allows tones rather than a single pitch. Shown once Output pin buzzer GPIO is set | . Store & Forward module . Buffers messages for nodes that were temporarily offline, then replays them when those nodes reconnect. Essential for meshes where nodes go in and out of range regularly — ensures messages aren’t lost during brief disconnections. A server needs an ESP32 with PSRAM or a Linux meshtasticd node. A node in the Router or Router Late role acts as a server even with the server setting off. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Előzmény-visszaadás maximum | Most stored messages returned per request. 0 uses 25 | 0 | . | Előzmény-visszaadás időablak | How far back, in minutes, stored messages are returned. 0 uses 240 | 0 | . | Rekordok száma | Most messages to store. 0 uses three quarters of the free PSRAM | 0 | . | Heartbeat jel | Periodically announce that this node is a store-and-forward server | Off | . | Szerver | Act as a store-and-forward server for the mesh | Off | . | Store and Forward Enabled | Turn store and forward on | Off | . Range Test module . Automated range testing tool for evaluating link quality between nodes. When enabled, the node periodically transmits test messages with incrementing counters. A receiver node logs these messages, allowing you to walk or drive away and later analyze at what distance messages stopped arriving. Range Test only works on a secured primary channel. As long as your primary channel still uses the default channel key, the interval and CSV controls stay disabled — you can still switch an already-enabled module off — and saving force-disables the module if the channel has reverted to public. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Hatótáv-teszt engedélyezve | Turn range testing on | Off | . | .CSV mentése a tárhelyre (csak ESP32) | Log received test data as a CSV on the node’s own filesystem. ESP32 nodes only | Off | . | Sender Interval | Time between test transmissions, chosen from a dropdown of fixed intervals. Unset stops sending | Nincs beállítva | . Telemetry module . Controls what telemetry data your node shares with the mesh. Telemetry includes device health (battery, uptime) and environmental sensor data (temperature, humidity, pressure). Each of the four metric groups has its own enable toggle and its own interval, so you can report battery health often and sensors rarely. The intervals run from 30 minutes to 72 hours. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Levegőminőség-metrika modul engedélyezve | Report particulate and CO₂ sensor data | Off | . | Levegőminőségi metrikák frissítési időköze | How often to report them | — | . | Eszköztelemetria küldése | Send device metrics to the mesh. When it is off, they go only to connected clients. Only shown on firmware 2.7.13 and newer | Off | . | Eszközmetrikák frissítési időköze | How often to report battery, uptime and channel utilization | — | . | Környezeti metrikák Fahrenheit-ben | Use °F on the device’s display. This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | Off | . | Környezeti metrika modul engedélyezve | Report the attached environment sensors | Off | . | Környezeti metrikák frissítési időköze | How often to report them | — | . | Energia-metrika modul engedélyezve | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | Off | . | Tápellátási metrikák frissítési időköze | How often to report them | — | . | Energia-metrikák megjelenítése képernyőn engedélyezve | Also show power readings on the device’s display | Off | . | Környezeti metrikák megjelenítése képernyőn | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | Off | . See Telemetry & Sensors for supported sensors and configuration recommendations. Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). Define a list of quick-send messages that can be transmitted without a phone connected — ideal for field use. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | Semmi | . | Üzenetek | Newline-separated list of messages | Üres | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | Rotary Encoder | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | Off | . | Harangjel küldése | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | Off | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | Off | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . Codec2 audio support for low-bandwidth voice communication over the mesh. This is an experimental feature that encodes voice into very small data packets using the Codec2 codec. It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | CODEC2 mintavételi ráta | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | Alapértelmezett | . | CODEC 2 engedélyezve | Turn the audio module on | Off | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | PTT pin | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . GPIO control over the mesh network. Allows a remote node to read or write GPIO pins on another node — useful for activating relays, reading switches, or controlling external hardware from a distance. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Nem definiált pinek elérésének engedélyezése | Allow access to any GPIO pin (security risk) | Off | . | Elérhető pinek | Up to 4 GPIO pins this node exposes for remote read/write | Semmi | . | Távoli hardver engedélyezve | Turn remote GPIO access on | Off | . Neighbor Info module . Broadcasts information about directly heard neighbors, enabling mesh topology mapping. Each enabled node periodically shares a list of the other nodes it can hear and their signal quality. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Szomszéd-információ engedélyezve | Turn neighbor broadcasting on | Off | . | Továbbítás LoRa-n keresztül | Also broadcast neighbor info over LoRa, not just MQTT and the connected app. Unavailable on a channel using the default key and name | Off | . | Frissítési időköz | How often to broadcast the neighbor list, in seconds. Minimum 4 hours | 0 (firmware default) | . See Local Mesh Discovery for how to use neighbor data for mesh topology exploration. Ambient Lighting module . Controls onboard NeoPixel or other addressable RGB LEDs on supported hardware. Can be used for visual status indicators, notification lights, or decorative effects. Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Áramerősség | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LED állapot | Turn the LED on or off | Off | . | Red / Green / Blue | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . Turns your node into a motion or door sensor alert system. When a GPIO pin detects a state change (motion detected, door opened), the node broadcasts an alert message over the mesh. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | Érzékelő szenzor engedélyezve | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | Off | . | Figyelt GPIO láb | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | Minimum time between alert broadcasts | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | Barátságos név | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Üres | . | Harangjel küldése | Include a bell character in alerts | Off | . | State Broadcast Interval | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | Nincs beállítva | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | High | . | Use Internal Pull-up | Enable the pin’s internal pull-up resistor | Off | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. Counts nearby devices by passively listening for probe requests that phones and laptops emit when scanning for networks. Available only on ESP32 devices. Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | Setting | Leírás | Alapértelmezett | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | Paxcounter engedélyezve | Turn people counting on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must both be off on the node for it to work | Off | . | Frissítési időköz | How often to report counts | — | . | WiFi Threshold (dBm) | Ignore Wi-Fi probes weaker than this, so distant devices aren’t counted | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . Status Message module . The status message has no module screen. It is edited with the rest of the node’s identity, on Settings — Radio & User. Mesh Beacon module . Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. TAK module . Team Awareness Kit integration for interoperability with ATAK and WinTAK. The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. See TAK Integration for detailed setup and usage.

On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Leállítás | Powers the node down | . | Gyári beállítások visszaállítása | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | NodeDB törlése | Clears the node database. 4869.title: الإدارة
4869.content: Remote Administration . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | Modify configuration. | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | Action | What it does | . | Set time | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | إعادة التشغيل | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Shutdown | Powers the node down | . | Factory reset | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | NodeDB reset | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. Backup & Restore . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. Advanced . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. Clean Node Database . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. Debug Panel . Opens the Packets and App logs tabs for viewing, filtering, and exporting diagnostic output. See Debug Logs for the full walkthrough. App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. حول . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. Acknowledgements . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Troubleshooting remote admin . | “Could not reach node — try again or move closer.” The target may be out of range or offline, or it doesn’t list your node’s public key as an admin key. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. Reconnect it from the Connections screen. | Changes not applying — some settings require a reboot to take effect. Try the Reboot action after saving. | .

4872.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4872.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Disabling unused modules reduces airtime, saves battery, and simplifies your configuration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. 4874.title: Administration
4874.content: Fjärradministration . Remote administration changes another node’s settings over the mesh. The target node must list your node’s public key as one of its Admin Key entries, set on its Settings → Security screen. | Tap the target node in the node list to open its detail screen. | In the Administration card, tap Remote Administration. The app first establishes a session with the node, showing Establishing remote session…, then opens its Settings. | Modify configuration. | Tap Save or Save & restart. The changes are sent over the mesh. | . Device Actions . Settings → Administration holds one-shot actions, each behind a confirmation dialog: . | Action | What it does | . | Ställ in tid | Sends your phone’s clock to the node | . | Starta om | Restarts the node | . | Reboot into DFU mode | Restarts an nRF52 node into its bootloader, where it stays off the mesh until new firmware is flashed or it is reset. On bootloader 2.6.0 and later it boots the installed firmware after 6 minutes with no update activity. Shown only for nRF52 nodes | . | Stäng av | Powers the node down | . | Återställ till standardinställningar | Returns every setting to its factory default | . | Nollställ NodeDB | Clears the node database. This dialog carries a Preserve Favorites? switch | . ⚠️ Warning: Factory reset erases all settings, channels, and keys, and cannot be undone. Before you reset, use Export configuration to save the node’s settings and Backup Keys on the Security screen to save its keys, so you can put both back afterwards. Säkerhetskopiering och återställning . Settings → Backup & Restore writes the connected node’s whole configuration to a file with Export configuration, and reads a saved file back in with Import configuration. Traffic Management settings are exported but not applied on import. Export before a factory reset, or to copy one node’s setup onto another. The section is shown for your own node only, not over remote admin. The same section backs up the app’s own data for a node: its messages and nodes as stored in the app, not the node’s settings. | Back up app data saves that data to a file named after the node and the date. | Restore app data replaces the app’s messages and nodes for that node with a backup, after a confirmation. It accepts only an undamaged backup made by an app with the same database version. The restore takes effect after you restart the app and reconnect to that node. | . Both disconnect the node first, after asking, and act on the data of the node that was connected. With no node connected they act on the most recently connected node. They stay disabled, with the line Connect to a radio first. There is no app data to back up or restore yet., until the app has stored data for some node. Advancerat . Settings → Advanced collects the tools that read or rewrite local state, and is likewise shown for your own node only: Firmware Update on OTA-capable hardware, Clean Node Database, TAK Server, Local Mesh Discovery, and the Debug Panel. Rensa noddatabas . Prunes nodes from your node database — from the app’s copy and from the node’s own, so this is not a display-only cleanup. The two filters combine rather than acting separately; the screen puts it as Selections are additive. | Clean up nodes last seen older than N days — always applied. The slider runs from 7 days to 365 and starts at 30; with Clean up only unknown nodes turned on, its floor drops to 0. | Clean up only unknown nodes — narrows the same purge to nodes that never sent their user info. The age limit still applies on top of it. | . The screen lists the nodes queued for deletion as you move the filters. Clean Now carries the purge out, after one more confirmation, and it can’t be undone. Favorited nodes, ignored nodes, and nodes with a public key heard in the last seven days are never removed, whatever the filters say — that is why the queued list can be shorter than you expect. Felsökningspanel . Opens the Packets and App logs tabs for viewing, filtering, and exporting diagnostic output. See Debug Logs for the full walkthrough. App Settings . The App section of the Settings screen configures the app rather than the node, and appears only when your own node is selected. It holds, in order: . | Allow analytics and crash reporting. — opt in or out of diagnostics. Google Play build only. | Provide phone location to mesh — share this phone’s position when the node has no GPS fix. It needs precise location: with approximate location allowed, turning it on asks for precise. | Compact encoding for Cyrillic — how look-alike characters in names are handled. | Language, Theme, and Units. Units is metric, imperial, or follow the system, and is the entry Units & Locale sends you to. | Show full message timestamps. | Device DB cache limit, which sets how much history is kept. | Export rangetest packets, Export all packets and Export node database. | Node Layout — how much detail each row of the node list shows. | Wi-Fi Provisioning for mPWRD-OS — see Connections. | Message Filter — hides incoming messages that contain words you list. With no words configured it does nothing. | System AI — appears only where app functions are available; see App Functions. | . A Permissions section sits above App, so a user who skipped a permission during onboarding can get back to it. Information sits below it, with Show Introduction, App Notifications, System Settings, About, and the app version. Help & Documentation closes the screen. Om . Settings → About carries the app’s own identity rather than the node’s, in three sections: . | What is Meshtastic? — a short description of the project. | Apps — opens with Need Hardware?, a rotating carousel of popular devices that links out to where to buy one. It also lists the GitHub repository, the running app version, and Acknowledgements (see the next section). | Project information — links to the website, to this documentation, and to the GNU GPL v3 license the app is released under. | . The footer states the copyright and that the app is free software with no warranty, which you may redistribute under the same license. Bekräftelser . Reached from About, this lists every open-source library the app ships, with its license, generated at build time by AboutLibraries. Troubleshooting remote admin . | “Could not reach node — try again or move closer.” The target may be out of range or offline, or it doesn’t list your node’s public key as an admin key. Check the Admin Key entries on the target node. | “Connect to a radio to administer remote nodes.” Your own node isn’t connected. Reconnect it from the Connections screen. | Changes not applying — some settings require a reboot to take effect. Try the Reboot action after saving. | .

4877.title: Sätted - moodulid & admin
4877.content: Konfi valikulisi funktsioonimooduleid ja teosta seadme haldamist. Moodulid laiendavad Meshtasticut spetsiaalsete võimalustega – igaüht saab eraldi lubada või keelata. Enable only the modules you use. Kasutamata moodulite keelamine vähendab eetriaega, säästab akut ja lihtsustab seadistamist. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Mooduli seaded kasutavad kaardipõhist paigutust koos lülitite, rippmenüüde, tekstiväljade ja liuguritega: . .

4878.title: Mooduli sätted
4878.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. Kasulik seadmetele, mis peavad sõnumi saabumisest füüsiliselt märku andma – eriti kasulik järelevalveta või välistingimustes paigaldamise korral. 4882.title: Settings — Modules & Admin
4882.content: Configure optional feature modules and perform device administration. Modules extend Meshtastic with specialized capabilities — each can be independently enabled or disabled. Enable only the modules you use. Unbenutzte Module auszuschalten verringert die Sendezeit, spart Batterie und vereinfacht deine Konfiguration. A module you expect can be missing for three reasons: your node’s role doesn’t enable it, your firmware is older than the release that added it, or the firmware build excludes it for this hardware. Module settings use a card-based layout with toggle switches, dropdowns, text fields, and sliders: . .

4883.title: Moduleinstellungen
4883.content: Every module lives under Settings → Module configuration. Saving a module screen restarts the node: the button reads Save & restart, and the node is unreachable for a few seconds afterwards. External Notification and Mesh Beacon are the exceptions: their button reads Save. External Notification may still restart the node for some changes, while a Mesh Beacon change applies without a restart. MQTT module . Bridges mesh messages to and from an MQTT broker for internet connectivity. This is how you extend your mesh beyond LoRa range or integrate with home automation systems. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Adresse | MQTT broker address | mqtt.meshtastic.org | . | Verschlüsselung aktiviert | Publish packets still encrypted with the channel key | On | . | JSON-Ausgabe aktiviert | Publish and consume MQTT messages as JSON. Shown only for a node on firmware older than 2.8, which removed JSON support, or while the setting is still on | Aus | . | Map Reporting | Publish position to the public map — see the map reporting card that follows | Aus | . | Proxy zu Client aktiviert | Let the connected app carry the node’s MQTT traffic, instead of the node reaching the broker itself | Aus | . | MQTT aktiviert | Turn the MQTT bridge on | Aus | . | MQTT proxy in this app | The app-side half of MQTT Client Proxy: whether this app acts as that relay. It shows whether the relay is running, and can be turned on only while MQTT Enabled and MQTT Client Proxy are both on. See MQTT | — | . | Passwort | Authentication password | The public broker’s | . | Hauptthema | Base MQTT topic path | msh | . | TLS aktiviert | Use a secure connection | Aus | . | Benutzername | Authentication username | The public broker’s | . Turning Map Reporting on reveals a consent card headed Consent to Share Unencrypted Node Data via MQTT, with an I agree. switch under it. The rest of the card doesn’t exist on screen until you agree: . | Einstellung | Beschreibung | . | Ich stimme zu. | Explicit consent to transmit your node data, including an approximate position, unencrypted. Map reporting doesn’t start without it | . | Map Publish Interval | How often to report. A dropdown of fixed intervals from 1 hour to 72 hours — nothing shorter is offered | . | Precision slider | The slider has no label of its own. It sets how coarsely your position is published, from 12 to 15; the line beneath reads ± the resulting distance, in your own units | . See MQTT for a detailed usage guide including encryption, privacy, and broker setup. Serial module . Enables serial port communication for external device integrations (GPS modules, sensors, or custom hardware). When enabled, the node’s serial port can send and receive protobuf or text data, allowing external microcontrollers or computers to interact with the mesh. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Serielle Baudrate | Port speed, from 110 Baud to 921600 Baud | Standardwert | . | Echo aktiviert | Echo packets you send back over the serial port | Aus | . | Serieller Modus | Which protocol the port speaks: Default, Simple, Protobufs, Text Message, NMEA Positions, or CalTopo, plus WS85, VE_DIRECT, MS_CONFIG, LOG and LOGTEXT under their firmware names | Standardwert | . | Seriellen Anschluss der Konsole überschreiben | Take over the port the debug console normally uses | Aus | . | Receive data (rxd) GPIO pin / Transmit data (txd) GPIO pin | GPIO pins for the serial connection | 0 | . | Serielle Schnittstelle aktiviert | Turn serial communication on | Aus | . | Zeitlimit erreicht | How long to wait before treating received data as a complete packet. 0 uses 250 ms | 0 | . External Notification module . Controls buzzer, LED, or vibration alerts on your node hardware. Useful for devices that need to physically signal when a message arrives — particularly helpful for unattended or outdoor installations. There are two independent triggers — an incoming message, and a received bell character — and each can drive the LED, the buzzer and the vibration motor separately, giving six toggles. The firmware turns the module on, and picks the outputs, on hardware that has a buzzer, vibration motor or notification LED; elsewhere everything starts off. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | . | Ausgabe LED aktiv hoch | Whether the LED pin is active high or low. Shown once Output pin GPIO is set | . | Alert when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a bell / Alert GPIO vibra motor when receiving a bell | Which outputs fire on a received bell character | . | Alert when receiving a message / Alert GPIO buzzer when receiving a message / Vibra Motor Alert | Which outputs fire on an incoming message | . | Externe Benachrichtigungen aktiviert | Master toggle for the module | . | GPIO Output Duration | How long a single alert lasts | . | Nervige Verzögerung | Keep repeating the alert for this long until it is acknowledged. Unset disables nagging | . | Ausgabe LED (GPIO) | Pin the LED is wired to | . | Ausgabe Summer (GPIO) | Pin the buzzer is wired to | . | Ausgabe Vibration (GPIO) | Pin the vibration motor is wired to | . | Klingelton | The tone played on a PWM buzzer, in RTTTL. Can be imported from a file | . | I2S als Buzzer verwenden | Send the alert through an I2S audio output instead | . | Benutze PWM Summer | Drive the buzzer with PWM, which allows tones rather than a single pitch. Shown once Output pin buzzer GPIO is set | . Store & Forward module . Buffers messages for nodes that were temporarily offline, then replays them when those nodes reconnect. Essential for meshes where nodes go in and out of range regularly — ensures messages aren’t lost during brief disconnections. A server needs an ESP32 with PSRAM or a Linux meshtasticd node. A node in the Router or Router Late role acts as a server even with the server setting off. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Verlauf Rückgabewert maximal | Most stored messages returned per request. 0 uses 25 | 0 | . | Zeitraum Rückgabewert | How far back, in minutes, stored messages are returned. 0 uses 240 | 0 | . | Anzahl Einträge | Most messages to store. 0 uses three quarters of the free PSRAM | 0 | . | Puls | Periodically announce that this node is a store-and-forward server | Aus | . | Server | Act as a store-and-forward server for the mesh | Aus | . | Speichern & Weiterleiten aktiviert | Turn store and forward on | Aus | . Range Test module . Automated range testing tool for evaluating link quality between nodes. When enabled, the node periodically transmits test messages with incrementing counters. A receiver node logs these messages, allowing you to walk or drive away and later analyze at what distance messages stopped arriving. Range Test only works on a secured primary channel. As long as your primary channel still uses the default channel key, the interval and CSV controls stay disabled — you can still switch an already-enabled module off — and saving force-disables the module if the channel has reverted to public. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Reichweitentest aktiviert | Turn range testing on | Aus | . | Speichere .CSV im Speicher (nur ESP32) | Log received test data as a CSV on the node’s own filesystem. ESP32 nodes only | Aus | . | Sendeintervall | Time between test transmissions, chosen from a dropdown of fixed intervals. Unset stops sending | Nicht konfiguriert | . Telemetry module . Controls what telemetry data your node shares with the mesh. Telemetry includes device health (battery, uptime) and environmental sensor data (temperature, humidity, pressure). Each of the four metric groups has its own enable toggle and its own interval, so you can report battery health often and sensors rarely. The intervals run from 30 minutes to 72 hours. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Modul Luftqualität aktiviert | Report particulate and CO₂ sensor data | Aus | . | Aktualisierungsintervall der Luftqualität | How often to report them | — | . | Gerätetelemetrie senden | Send device metrics to the mesh. When it is off, they go only to connected clients. Only shown on firmware 2.7.13 and newer | Aus | . | Aktualisierungsintervall für Gerätedaten | How often to report battery, uptime and channel utilization | — | . | Umweltdaten in Fahrenheit | Use °F on the device’s display. This is the node’s screen only — the app follows your phone’s locale, see Units & Locale | Aus | . | Modul Umweltdaten aktiviert | Report the attached environment sensors | Aus | . | Aktualisierungsintervall für Umweltdaten | How often to report them | — | . | Modul Energiedaten aktiviert | Report the per-channel voltage and current readings | Aus | . | Aktualisierungsintervall für Energiedaten | How often to report them | — | . | Energiedatenanzeige aktiviert | Also show power readings on the device’s display | Aus | . | Umweltdatenanzeige aktiviert | Also show environment readings on the device’s display | Aus | . See Telemetry & Sensors for supported sensors and configuration recommendations. Canned Message module . Pre-configured messages accessible from the node’s physical buttons (for nodes with rotary encoders, keypads, or similar input hardware). Define a list of quick-send messages that can be transmitted without a phone connected — ideal for field use. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Clockwise Rotary Event / Counterclockwise Rotary Event / Encoder Press Event | Which key event each encoder action produces: None, Up, Down, Left, Right, Select, Back, or Cancel | Keins | . | Nachrichten | Newline-separated list of messages | Leer | . | Pin A / Pin B / Press Pin | The three pins the rotary encoder is wired to | 0 | . | Drehgeber | Use a rotary encoder as the input device | Aus | . | Glocke senden | Send a bell character alongside the message, so a receiving node’s External Notification module can sound | Aus | . | Up/Down/Select Input | A separate, simpler input scheme using up/down/select buttons rather than an encoder | Aus | . Some boards with built-in encoders or keys come with the input settings filled in. Two older fields, Canned message enabled and Allow input source, appear only for a node on firmware older than 2.7, or while they still hold a value. Audio module . Codec2 audio support for low-bandwidth voice communication over the mesh. This is an experimental feature that encodes voice into very small data packets using the Codec2 codec. It needs specific hardware, an I2S microphone and speaker, and the voice quality is low. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | CODEC2 Abtastrate | Codec2 bitrate, from 450 bps to 3200 bps. Lower rates use less bandwidth and give poorer audio | Standardwert | . | CODEC 2 aktiviert | Turn the audio module on | Aus | . | I2S Clock Pin | GPIO pin for the I2S bit clock | 0 | . | I2S Data In Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data in | 0 | . | I2S Data Out Pin | GPIO pin for I2S data out | 0 | . | I2S Word Select Pin | GPIO pin for I2S word select | 0 | . | GPIO Pin PTT | GPIO pin for the push-to-talk button. 0 uses GPIO 39 | 0 | . Remote Hardware module . GPIO control over the mesh network. Allows a remote node to read or write GPIO pins on another node — useful for activating relays, reading switches, or controlling external hardware from a distance. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on Allow undefined pin access gives remote nodes access to all GPIO pins, which could interfere with the node’s own hardware. Turn it on only on dedicated GPIO nodes. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Erlaube undefinierten Pin-Zugriff | Allow access to any GPIO pin (security risk) | Aus | . | Verfügbare Pins | Up to 4 GPIO pins this node exposes for remote read/write | Keins | . | Einstellung entfernte Hardware | Turn remote GPIO access on | Aus | . Neighbor Info module . Broadcasts information about directly heard neighbors, enabling mesh topology mapping. Each enabled node periodically shares a list of the other nodes it can hear and their signal quality. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Nachbarinformationen aktiviert | Turn neighbor broadcasting on | Aus | . | Übertragen über LoRa | Also broadcast neighbor info over LoRa, not just MQTT and the connected app. Unavailable on a channel using the default key and name | Aus | . | GPS Abfrageintervall | How often to broadcast the neighbor list, in seconds. Minimum 4 hours | 0 (firmware default) | . See Local Mesh Discovery for how to use neighbor data for mesh topology exploration. Ambient Lighting module . Controls onboard NeoPixel or other addressable RGB LEDs on supported hardware. Can be used for visual status indicators, notification lights, or decorative effects. Pick the color with the swatch’s Preset colors row or the Red, Green and Blue sliders. Advanced opens number fields for the same three values. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Stromstärke | LED drive current, 0 to 31 | 10 | . | LED Zustand | Turn the LED on or off | Aus | . | Red / Green / Blue | Individual color channel values, 0 to 255 | Derived from the node number | . Detection Sensor module . Turns your node into a motion or door sensor alert system. When a GPIO pin detects a state change (motion detected, door opened), the node broadcasts an alert message over the mesh. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | Erkennungssensor aktiviert | Turn the detection sensor on. It also has to be on for nodes that receive its alerts or chart its log | Aus | . | Zu überwachender GPIO-Pin | GPIO pin connected to the sensor. 0 disables the module | 0 | . | Minimum time between detection broadcasts | Minimum time between alert broadcasts | 0, which the firmware treats as 1 hour (12 hours on Router roles) | . | Anzeigename | Custom name for this sensor, used in its messages | Leer | . | Glocke senden | Include a bell character in alerts | Aus | . | Übertragungsintervall | How often to send the sensor’s state whether or not anything was detected. Unset sends only on detection | Nicht konfiguriert | . | Trigger Type | How the pin’s state maps to a detection event: High, Low, Rising Edge, Falling Edge, Either Edge High, or Either Edge Low | Hoch | . | Use Internal Pull-up | Enable the pin’s internal pull-up resistor | Aus | . Paxcounter module . People counter using Wi-Fi and BLE probe requests. Counts nearby devices by passively listening for probe requests that phones and laptops emit when scanning for networks. Available only on ESP32 devices. Counts are approximate, since one person may carry several devices, so the module suits estimating foot traffic at trailheads or event venues. | Einstellung | Beschreibung | Standardwert | . | BLE Threshold (dBm) | The same cut-off for BLE advertisements | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . | Besucherzähler aktiviert | Turn people counting on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth must both be off on the node for it to work | Aus | . | GPS Abfrageintervall | How often to report counts | — | . | WiFi Threshold (dBm) | Ignore Wi-Fi probes weaker than this, so distant devices aren’t counted | 0, which the firmware treats as −80 dBm | . Status Message module . The status message has no module screen. It is edited with the rest of the node’s identity, on Settings — Radio & User. Mesh Beacon module . Broadcasts an invitation to your mesh, and receives invitations from others. The entry appears only on nodes running firmware 2.8.0 or newer. See Local Mesh Discovery for the full walkthrough. TAK module . Team Awareness Kit integration for interoperability with ATAK and WinTAK. The entry is labeled TAK (ATAK). Two things have to be true before it appears in the module list: the node runs firmware 2.8.0 or newer, and its Device Role on Settings → Device configuration → Device is set to TAK or TAK Tracker. Siehe TAK Integration für detaillierte Einrichtung und Nutzung.

4887.title: Settings — Radio & User
4887.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

4888.title: How these screens work
4888.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

4889.title: User Settings
4889.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Nastavení | Popis | Výchozí | . | Licencované amatérské rádio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Vypnuto | . | Dlouhé jméno | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Krátké jméno | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Stavová zpráva | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. 4891.title: LoRa nastavení
4891.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK do MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Vypnuto | . | Přepsat pracovní cyklus | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Vypnuto | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Vypnuto | . | Předvolby | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Region | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | Zvýšené zesílení přijímače (RX) | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Vysílání povoleno | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Vysílací výkon | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Použít předvolbu | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Rychlost | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

4897.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Nastavení | Popis | Výchozí | . | Administrátorský klíč | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Žádný | . | Záloha klíčů | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Ladící protokol API povolen | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Vypnuto | . | Smazat zálohu klíče | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Řízený režim | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Úroveň ochrany | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Veřejný klíč | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Obnovit soukromý klíč | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Obnovit klíče | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Sériová komunikace | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Zbývající počet restartů | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hodiny do vypršení platnosti | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Limit relace (minuty) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

4901.title: How these screens work
4901.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

4910.title: Configuração de Segurança
4910.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Descrição | Predefinição | . | Chave do Administrador | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Nenhum | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | API de histórico de depuração ativada | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Modo Administrado | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Chave pública | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Consola de série | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

4914.title: How these screens work
4914.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Descripció | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Descripció | Default | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | None | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. 4927.title: How these screens work
4927.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

4930.title: LoRa Config
4930.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Opis | Default | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Regija | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Speed | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.
