4943.title: LoRa Config
4943.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Lýsing | Default | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Svæði | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Speed | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

4949.title: Security Config
4949.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Lýsing | Default | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | None | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Managed Device | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Private Key | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Public Key | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

4952.title: Settings — Radio & User
4952.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

4953.title: How these screens work
4953.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

4954.title: User Settings
4954.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Beskrivelse | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Offentlig nøkkel | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

4965.title: Settings — Radio & User
4965.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

4966.title: How these screens work
4966.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

4967.title: User Settings
4967.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Açıklaması | Varsayılan | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Uzun Ad | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Kısa Ad | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Boş | . | Mesaj gönderilemez | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Hata ayıklama kaydı API’si etkin | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Yönetilen Mod | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Özel Anahtar | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Genel Anahtar | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Seri konsol | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

4979.title: How these screens work
4979.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. 設定には、標準的な設定コントロール（ドロップダウン、トグル、スライダー）を使用します： . | コントロール | スクリーンショット | . | ドロップダウン | | . | トグル | | . | スライダー | | .

4982.doc: 設定：無線機とユーザー
4982.title: LoRa設定
4982.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. 詳しくは、meshtastic.org の リージョン設定ガイド を参照してください。 . | 設定項目 | 説明 | デフォルト | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | 符号化レート | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | 周波数の上書き | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | 周波数スロット | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | ホップ数 | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | MQTT を無視 | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | MQTTを許可 | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | オフ | . | デューティサイクルを上書き | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | オフ | . | PAファン無効 | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | オフ | . | プリセット | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | リージョン | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | 未設定（要設定） | . | RX ブーストゲイン | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | 拡散率 | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | 送信を有効化 | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | 送信出力 | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0（リージョン最大） | . | プリセットを使用 | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa はノイズフロアを下回る信号でも復調できるため、より負の大きい限界値ほど、そのプリセットは弱くノイズの多い信号に耐えられます（より遠くまで届きます）。詳しい説明は、信号メーターの仕組み を参照してください。 . | プリセット | 距離 | 速度 | SNR 限界 | 最適な用途 | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | 見通しのある高密度な都市部。データ量の多い用途 | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | 都市の住宅街。数ブロック以内の建物 | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | 郊外の短距離。中程度の建物密度 | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | 郊外エリア。中程度の建物密度 | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | 郊外・地方。中程度の距離で低速 | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Long Fast と同程度の距離だが 500 kHz 帯域幅。スループットが速い | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | 一般用途（デフォルト）：距離と速度のバランスが良い | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | 起伏のある地方。ときどき使う用途 | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD 帯（125 kHz 帯域幅）。Medium Fast に相当 | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD 帯（125 kHz 帯域幅）。Long Fast に相当 | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz 帯（62.5 kHz 帯域幅）。他のデバイスとの干渉を避ける | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz 帯（62.5 kHz 帯域幅）。Long Fast に相当 | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . モデムプリセットは、距離とデータ速度の基本的なトレードオフを制御します： . | 遅いプリセットは拡散をより多く使い、より弱い信号レベルでも復調できるようにします（SNR 限界が低い）。これは、より遠くまで届く一方で、1 秒あたりのバイト数が少ないことを意味します。 | 速いプリセットは 1 回の送信でより多くのデータを詰め込みますが、復調にはより強い信号が必要です。 | . 実用的な指針： . | 都市部のメッシュ（多数のノード、短距離）： Long Fast（デフォルト）または Short Fast を使用します。速度が速いほど、多くのノードがチャンネルを共有するときの電波利用時間の輻輳が減ります。 | 地方・まばらなメッシュ（少数のノード、長距離）： Long Moderate を使用します。ノードが離れている場合は、速度よりも距離が重要です。 | EU 866／868 MHz の規制対応： Lite Fast、Lite Slow、Narrow Fast、Narrow Slow を使用します。これらは、より狭い帯域幅で EU の SRD／868 MHz 帯に最適化されています。 | 固定インフラのリンク： 良好なアンテナと見通しがある専用のポイントツーポイントリンクには、Short Turbo または Long Turbo を使用します。 | 混在した環境： Long Fast のままにします。これはコミュニティのデフォルトで、地域内の他のユーザーとの互換性を確保します。 | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. 高所（丘の上、屋上）にあると、実効的な距離が大幅に伸びます。適切に設置された Long Fast のルーターは、地上に置かれた Long Slow のノードを上回ることがよくあります。 .

Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | オフ | . | 秘密鍵 | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | 保護レベル | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | 鍵を復元 | バックアップした鍵をノードに書き戻します（バックアップがある場合に利用可能） | — | . | シリアルコンソール | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. 4990.title: Settings — Radio & User
4990.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

4991.title: How these screens work
4991.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

4992.title: User Settings
4992.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

These settings set the node’s role on the mesh and its local hardware behavior. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Button GPIO / Buzzer GPIO | Advanced: which pins the user button and the PWM buzzer are wired to | 0 (board default) | . | Device Role | Node behavior: Client, Client Mute, Client Hidden, Client Base, Router, Router Late, Tracker, Sensor, TAK, TAK Tracker, or Lost and Found. The description of the selected role appears under the field. Choosing Router or Router Late opens a dialog where you confirm you have read the device-role guidance before Accept is enabled | Client | . | Disable LED Heartbeat | Controls the blinking status LED. Despite the label, the switch is on while the LED blinks | On (LED blinks) | . | Double Tap as Button | Treat a double tap on a supported accelerometer as a button press | Off | . | Node Info Broadcast Interval | How often the node re-announces itself. A dropdown of fixed intervals: Unset, then 3 to 72 hours | 3 hours | . | Rebroadcast Mode | Which packets the node relays: All, All Skip Decoding, Local Only, Known Only, None, or Core Portnums Only. 4994.title: LoRa Config
4994.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Region | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Speed | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

These control the node’s own screen, not the app’s. | Setting | Description | Default | . | 12 Hour Clock | Show the node’s clock as 12-hour rather than 24-hour | Off | . | Always point north | Locks the compass rose north-up instead of rotating it with your heading. Independent of Compass Orientation — neither replaces the other | Off | . | Bold Heading | Draw the screen’s heading text in bold | Off | . | Carousel Interval | How often the node moves to its next screen on its own: Unset (never), or 15 seconds to 15 minutes | Unset | . | Compass Orientation | Rotation offset for the compass rose: 0°, 90°, 180° or 270°, each with an Inverted variant | 0° | . | Display Mode | Screen layout: Default 128x64 screen layout, Optimized for 2 color displays, Inverted top bar for 2 color displays, or TFT Full Color Displays | Default, or color on nodes with a color screen | . | Display Units | Metric or Imperial on the node’s screen | Metric | . | Flip Screen | Flip the display for an inverted mounting | Off | . | OLED Type | Overrides automatic OLED detection: Detect Automatically, SSD1306, SH1106, SH1107, SH1107 128x128, or SH1107 Rotated | Detect Automatically | . | Screen on for | How long the display stays lit after a button press or a received message: 15 seconds to 1 hour, or Always On | 10 minutes | . | Wake Screen on tap or motion | Light the screen when the node is tapped or moved. Needs an accelerometer | Off | .

4996.title: Position Config
4996.content: On Settings → Device configuration → Position. These settings decide where the node’s position comes from and how often it is shared. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Broadcast Interval | The longest the node goes without broadcasting its position: Unset, or 1 minute to 72 hours | 1 hour | . | Fixed Position | Broadcast a manually entered Latitude, Longitude and Altitude instead of a live GPS fix. Set from current phone location fills them in | Off | . | GPS Enable GPIO / GPS Receive GPIO / GPS Transmit GPIO | Advanced: the pins an add-on GPS module is wired to. Hidden on boards whose maker wired the GPS, unless a pin already holds a value | 0 | . | GPS Mode | Enabled, Disabled, or Not Present. Hidden while Fixed Position is on | Depends on the hardware | . | Minimum Distance | In meters. With Smart Position on, how far you must move before a broadcast is considered | 100 m | . | Minimum Interval | With Smart Position on, the shortest gap between broadcasts once the distance is met | 5 minutes | . | Position Flags | A group of checkboxes choosing which fields ride along with a position, such as altitude, its reference and precision, satellites in view, and timestamp | Altitude, Altitude is Mean Sea Level, Vehicle speed, Vehicle heading, DOP, Number of satellites | . | Smart Position | Broadcast based on movement rather than purely on the clock | On | . | Update Interval | How often the node asks its GPS for a fix. Hidden while Fixed Position is on | 2 minutes | .

4997.title: Power Config
4997.content: On Settings → Device configuration → Power. These settings trade battery life against availability. | Setting | Description | Default | . | ADC multiplier override | Turn on a manual correction for battery-voltage readings | Off | . | ADC Override | The correction factor itself, shown only while the override is on | — | . | Battery INA_2XX I2C address | Address of an external INA-series power sensor, if fitted | 0 | . | Minimum wake time | The shortest time the node stays awake once woken | 10 seconds | . | Power Saving | Sleep as much as possible. On the Tracker and Sensor roles this includes the LoRa radio. Not for a node you use with the app, or one without a user button | Off | . | Shutdown on Power Loss | How long after external power is removed before the node powers off. Unset disables it, and values under 30 seconds are raised to 30 | Unset | . | Super deep sleep duration | How long the deepest sleep state lasts | — | . | Wait for Bluetooth Duration | How long to wait for a phone to connect before sleeping | 1 minute | .

4998.title: Network Config
4998.content: On Settings → Device configuration → Network, on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet. When the node is on a network, a Current connections: card at the top shows its Wi-Fi IP: or Ethernet IP:. ⚠️ Warning: Turning on WiFi Enabled or Ethernet Enabled ends the Bluetooth connection between your phone and the node. Reconnect over the network afterwards from the Connections screen, or turn Wi-Fi off again from the node’s own screen or over USB. Saving this screen also always reboots the node. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Address Mode | DHCP, or Static with the four address fields that follow | DHCP | . | Ethernet Enabled | Use a wired connection. Shown only on hardware that has Ethernet | Off | . | IP / Gateway / Subnet / DNS | The static address, shown only when Address Mode is Static | — | . | NTP Server | Time synchronization server | meshtastic.pool.ntp.org | . | Password | Network password. Appears only once WiFi Enabled is on | — | . | Rsyslog Server | Remote logging server | — | . | SSID | Network name to connect to. Appears only once WiFi Enabled is on. Scan Wi-Fi QR code fills it and Password from a standard Wi-Fi QR code; on Android, holding the phone against a Wi-Fi NFC tag while this screen is open fills them the same way, and the app offers to open system settings if NFC is turned off | — | . | UDP broadcasting | Share mesh traffic with other nodes over the local network | Off | . | WiFi Enabled | Connect the node to Wi-Fi | Off | .

4999.title: Bluetooth Config
4999.content: On Settings → Device configuration → Bluetooth, on nodes with Bluetooth. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Bluetooth Enabled | Turn the node’s Bluetooth on or off | On, except on some nodes with a color screen | . | Fixed Pin | PIN code for pairing, used with FIXED_PIN. Must be exactly six digits — the field rejects anything else | 123456 | . | Pairing Mode | Listed by firmware name: RANDOM_PIN, FIXED_PIN, or NO_PIN | RANDOM_PIN on nodes with a screen, FIXED_PIN on nodes without one | .

5000.title: Security Config
5000.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Description | Default | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | None | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Managed Device | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Private Key | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Public Key | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5013.title: 보안 설정
5013.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | 설명 | 기본값 | . | Admin 키 | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | 없음 | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | 관리 모드 | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | 개인 키 | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | 공개 키 | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | 개인 키 다시 생성하기 | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | 시리얼 콘솔 | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5017.title: How these screens work
5017.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5018.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Descripción | Por defecto | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Nombre largo | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Nombre Corto | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Vacío | . | No se puede enviar mensajes | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5029.title: Settings — Radio & User
5029.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5030.title: How these screens work
5030.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5031.title: User Settings
5031.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Περιγραφή | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5033.title: LoRa Config
5033.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Περιγραφή | Default | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Περιφέρεια | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Speed | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5043.title: How these screens work

Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .
