5046.title: LoRa 配置
5046.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | 说明 | 默认 | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | 编码率 | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | 频率覆盖 | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | 频率时隙 | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | 节点数 | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | 忽略 MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | 使用MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | 关闭 | . | 覆盖占空比 | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | 关闭 | . | PA风扇已禁用 | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | 关闭 | . | 预设 | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | 区域 | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX 增益 | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | 扩散因子 | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | 启用传输 | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | 发送强度 | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | 使用预设 | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | 速度 | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Опис | За замовчуванням | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Швидкість кодування | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Перевизначити частоту | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Ігнорувати обмеження завантаженості каналу | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | Вентилятор вимкнений | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Пресети | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Регіон | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | Підсилення передачі | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Показник розширення сигналу | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Передача активована | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Потужність передачі | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Використовувати пресет | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Швидкість | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5065.title: Налаштування безпеки
5065.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Опис | За замовчуванням | . | Ключ адміністратора | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Жоден | . | Резервні ключі | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | API журналу відладки увімкнено | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Керований режим | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Приватний ключ | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Відкритий ключ | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Згенерувати закритий ключ | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Серійна консоль | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5068.title: Settings — Radio & User
5068.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5069.title: How these screens work
5069.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5070.title: User Settings
5070.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Descrición | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5078.title: Security Config
5078.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Descrición | Default | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | None | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Managed Device | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Private Key | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Public Key | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5082.title: How these screens work
5082.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Descriere | Prestabilit | . | Radioamator autorizat | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Netransmisibil | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5095.title: How these screens work
5095.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5098.title: LoRa Config
5098.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Aprašymas | Default | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Regionas | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Speed | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5111.title: Настройка LoRa
5111.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. Смотрите руководство по настройке региона на сайте meshtastic.org для получения подробной информации. | Настройка | Описание | По умолчанию | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Частота кодирования | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Переопределить частоту | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Частота слота | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Количество прыжков | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Игнорировать MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | ОК в MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Выкл | . | Переопределить рабочий цикл | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Выкл | . | PA вентилятор выключен | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Выкл | . | Шаблоны | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Регион / Страна | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Не установлено (необходимо настроить) | . | Усиление RX | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Коэффициент распространения | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Передача включена | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Мощность передатчика | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (максимум региона) | . | Использовать шаблон | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa может декодировать сигналы ниже уровня шума, поэтому более отрицательный предел означает, что пресет допускает более слабый, шумный сигнал (больший радиус действия). Смотрите Как работает измеритель сигнала для полного объяснения. | Предустановка | Диапазон | Скорость | Предел SNR | Лучше всего для | . | Short Turbo | ~1 км | 21.9 кб/с | −7.5 дБ | Плотная городская застройка с прямой видимостью; приложения, требующие высокой передачи данных | . | Short Fast | ~3 км | 10.9 кб/с | −7.5 дБ | Городские районы; здания в пределах нескольких кварталов | . | Short Slow | ~5 км | 6.25 kbps | -10 дБ | Пригородная зона с коротким диапазоном; умеренная плотность застройки | . | Medium Fast | ~5 км | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 дБ | Пригородные районы; умеренная плотность застройки | . | Medium Slow | ~8 км | 1.95 kbps | -15 дБ | Пригородный/сельский; умеренный диапазон со сниженной скоростью | . | Long Turbo | ~10 км | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 дБ | Диапазон, похожий на Long Fast, но с полосой пропускания 500 кГц; более высокая пропускная способность | . | Long Fast | ~10 км | 1.1 кб/с | −17.5 дБ | Общее использование (по умолчанию) — сбалансированный диапазон и скорость | . | Long Moderate | ~20 км | 0.34 кб/с | −17.5 дБ | Сельская местность с некоторым рельефом; случайное использование | . | Lite Fast | ~5 км | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 дБ | Диапазон RU 866 МГц SRD (ширина полосы 125 кГц); аналогично Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 км | 0.98 kbps | -15 дБ | Диапазон RU 866 МГц SRD (ширина полосы 125 кГц); аналогично Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 км | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 дБ | Диапазон RU 868 МГц (полоса пропускания 62,5 кГц); предотвращает помехи с другими устройствами | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 км | 1.30 kbps | -10 дБ | Диапазон RU 868 МГц (ширина полосы 62,5 кГц); аналогично Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 км | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 дБ | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 км | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 дБ | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 км | 0.33 kbps | -10 дБ | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 км | 0.18 кб/с | −20 дБ | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ км | 0.09 кб/с | −20 дБ | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . Предустановка модема управляет основным компромиссом между дальностью и скоростью передачи данных: . | Медленные предустановки используют большее распространение, что позволяет декодировать сигналы при более слабых уровнях сигнала (ниже порога SNR). Это означает большую дальность, но меньше байт в секунду. | Быстрые предустановки передают больше данных за одну передачу, но требуют более сильного сигнала для декодирования. | . Практическое руководство: . | Городская сеть (много нод, короткие расстояния): Используй Long Fast (по умолчанию) или Short Fast. Более высокая скорость означает меньшее переполнение канала эфирного времени, когда многие ноды используют канал. | Сельская/разреженная сеть (мало нод, большие расстояния): Используй Long Moderate. Дальность важнее скорости, когда ноды находятся далеко друг от друга. | Соответствие нормативным требованиям RU 866/868 МГц: Используй Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast или Narrow Slow — они оптимизированы для диапазонов RU SRD/868 МГц с более узкой полосой пропускания. | Фиксированные инфраструктурные связи: Используй Short Turbo или Long Turbo для выделенных соединений точка-точка с хорошими антеннами и прямой видимостью. | Смешанные среды: Используй Long Fast — это настройка по умолчанию в сообществе и она обеспечит совместимость с другими в вашем регионе. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Преимущество высоты (вершина холма, крыша) значительно увеличивает эффективную дальность. Хорошо размещённый маршрутизатор с Long Fast часто может превзойти наземную ноду с Long Slow.

5117.title: Настройки безопасности
5117.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Настройка | Описание | По умолчанию | . | Ключ администратора | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Отсутствует | . | Резервное копирование | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | API журнала отладки включен | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Выкл | . | Удалить резервную копию ключа | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Управляемый режим | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Выкл | . | Приватный ключ | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Уровень защиты | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Публичный ключ | Публичный ключ твоей ноды (только для чтения) | Derived from the private key | . | Пересоздать приватный ключ | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Восстановить ключи | Запишисать сохранённые ключи обратно на ноду (доступно, как только есть резервная копия) | — | . | Консоль COM-порта | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | Что она делает | . | Осталось загрузок | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Часов до истечения | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Ограничение сессии (минуты) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5120.title: How these screens work
5120.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5123.title: Configuration LoRa
5123.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Description | Par défaut | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Taux de codage | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Remplacer la fréquence | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Slot de fréquence | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Nombre de sauts | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignorer MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK vers MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Éteint | . | Autoriser le dépassement du temps d’émission autorisé par heure | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Éteint | . | Ventilateur PA désactivé | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Éteint | . | Préréglages | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Région | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | Gain RX Boosté | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Facteur de propagation | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmission activée | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Puissance d’émission | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Utiliser un préréglage | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Vitesse | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5129.title: Configuration de sécurité
5129.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Description | Par défaut | . | Clé Admin | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Aucun | . | Sauvegarder les clés | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | API de journalisation de débogage activée | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Éteint | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Mode géré | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Éteint | . | Clé privée | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Clé publique | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Régénérer la clé privée | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Console série | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Heures jusqu’à expiration | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Limite de sessions (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5132.title: Settings — Radio & User
5132.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5133.title: How these screens work
5133.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5134.title: User Settings
5134.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Deskripsyon | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5142.title: Security Config
5142.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Deskripsyon | Default | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Pa gen | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Managed Device | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Private Key | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Public Key | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5146.title: How these screens work
5146.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5147.title: Paramètres utilisateur
5147.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. | Setting | Description | . | Nom long | Your display name (up to 39 characters) | . | Nom court | 4-character abbreviated name | . | Statut du message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node — up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, and is absent otherwise | . | Non joignable par message | Marks the node as one nobody should try to message — for an unmonitored or infrastructure node. Other clients hide it from the contact list. Needs supporting firmware | . | Licensed amateur node (Ham) | Enable if you hold an amateur node license (permits higher power). Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign and adds a separate Long Name field; over remote admin the field stays Long Name | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5152.title: How these screens work
5152.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5153.title: User Settings
5153.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Popis | Predvolené | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Dlhé Meno | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Krátke Meno | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.
