5155.title: Konfigurácia LoRa
5155.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Popis | Predvolené | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ignore MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Región | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Transmit Enabled | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Use Preset | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Rýchlosť | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5161.title: Security Config
5161.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Popis | Predvolené | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Žiadny | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Managed Device | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Súkromný kľúč | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Verejný kľúč | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Serial Console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0,18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Impostazione | Descrizione | Predefinito | . | Chiave Amministratore | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Nessuno | . | Backup chiavi | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Livello di protezione | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Chiave Pubblica | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Rigenera Chiavi Private | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Console seriale | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Avvii rimanenti | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Ore alla scadenza | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Limite di sessione (minuti) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5177.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5178.title: How these screens work
5178.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | תיאור | Default | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5191.title: How these screens work
5191.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | 螢幕截圖 | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5194.title: LoRa規劃
5194.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | 設定 | 描述說明 | 默認 | . | 頻寬 (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | 編碼率 | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | 手動設定頻率 | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | 頻率槽 | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | 中繼次數 | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | 忽略 MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | 將消息轉發至MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | 覆蓋工作週期/佔空比 | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | 停用PA風扇 | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | 預設配置 | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | 地區 | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | 接收增益提升 | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | 擴頻因子 | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | 已啟用發射 | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | 傳輸功率 | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | 使用預設值 | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | 範圍 | 速度 | SNR Limit | Best For | . | 短 Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | 短 快 | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | 短 慢 | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | 中等快 | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | 中等慢 | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | 長度中等的 | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | 漫長且緩慢 | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | 非常緩慢 | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5203.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5204.title: How these screens work
5204.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Екранна снимка | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5207.title: Конфигуриране на LoRa
5207.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Настройка | Описание | По подразбиране | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Честотен слот | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Брой отскоци | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Игнориране на MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Предварително зададени | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Регион | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | RX Boosted Gain | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Spread Factor | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Предаването е активирано | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Мощност на предаване | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Използване на предварително зададени настройки | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Диапазон | Скорост | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Tärkeää: Käyttö väärällä alueasetuksella voi rikkoa paikallisia radiomääräyksiä. Katso alueasetusten määritysopas meshtastic.org-sivustolta saadaksesi lisätietoja. | Asetus | Kuvaus | Oletus | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | Esiasetuksesta | . | Koodausnopeus | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. Suurempi virheenkorjaus lisää lähetysaikaa | Esiasetuksesta | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Taajuuden ohitus | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (käytä laskettua arvoa) | . | Taajuuspaikka | Määrittää, mitä alueen taajuusväliä käytetään. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automaattinen) | . | Hyppyjen määrä | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Ohita MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | MQTT päällä | Salli yhdyskäytävien välittää pakettisi MQTT:hen | Pois | . | Ohita käyttöaste (Duty Cycle) | Ohittaa alueen lähetysajan käyttörajoituksen. Laitonta useimmilla alueilla. Ota käyttöön vain, jos radioamatöörilupasi sallii sen | Pois | . | PA tuuletin pois käytöstä | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Pois | . | Esiasetukset | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Alue | Taajuusalueen sääntelyalue. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Ei asetettu (on määritettävä) | . | RX tehostettu vahvistus | Lisävastaanottovahvistus SX126x-radioille. Kuluttaa hieman enemmän virtaa | Käytössä | . | Levennyskerroin (Spread Factor) | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | Esiasetuksesta | . | Lähetys käytössä | Tämän poistaminen käytöstä tekee radiosta vain vastaanottavan | Käytössä | . | Lähetysteho | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (alueen enimmäisteho) | . | Käytä esiasetusta | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | Käytössä | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa pystyy purkamaan signaaleja kohinatason alapuolelta, joten negatiivisempi raja tarkoittaa, että esiasetus sietää heikomman ja kohinaisemman signaalin (suurempi kantama). Katso Miten signaalimittari toimii saadaksesi täydellisen selityksen. | Esiasetus | Kantama | Nopeus | SNR-raja | Paras käyttöön | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Tiheä kaupunkiympäristö suoralla näköyhteydellä; paljon dataa siirtävät sovellukset | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Kaupunkialueet, rakennuksia muutaman korttelin säteellä | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Lyhyen kantaman esikaupunkialueet; kohtalainen rakennustiheys | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Esikaupunkialueet; kohtalainen rakennustiheys | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Esikaupunki-/maaseutualueet; kohtalainen kantama ja hitaampi nopeus | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Samankaltainen kantama kuin Long Fast -asetuksella, mutta 500 kHz:n kaistanleveydellä; suurempi tiedonsiirtonopeus | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | Yleiskäyttö (oletus) — tasapaino kantaman ja nopeuden välillä | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Maaseutualueet, joissa on jonkin verran maastonmuotoja; satunnainen käyttö | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD -alue (125 kHz BW); verrattavissa Medium Fast -asetukseen | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD -alue (125 kHz BW); verrattavissa Long Fast -asetukseen | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz -alue (62,5 kHz BW); välttää häiriöitä muiden laitteiden kanssa | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz -alue (62,5 kHz BW); verrattavissa Long Fast -asetukseen | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . Modeemiesiasetus määrittää tärkeimmän kompromissin kantaman ja tiedonsiirtonopeuden välillä: . | Hitaammat esiasetukset käyttävät enemmän hajautusta, jolloin signaali voidaan purkaa heikommilla signaalitasoilla (alempi SNR-raja). Tämä tarkoittaa pidempää kantamaa, mutta vähemmän tavuja sekunnissa. | Nopeammat esiasetukset siirtävät enemmän dataa, mutta vaativat vahvemman signaalin purkamista varten. | . Käytännön ohje: . | Kaupunkiverkko (paljon radioita, lyhyet etäisyydet): Käytä Long Fast -asetusta (oletus) tai Short Fast -asetusta. Suurempi nopeus tarkoittaa vähemmän käyttöasteruuhkaa, kun monet radiot jakavat saman kanavan. | Maaseutu tai harva verkko (vähän radioita, pitkät etäisyydet): Käytä Long Moderate -asetusta. Kantama on tärkeämpi kuin nopeus, kun radiot ovat kaukana toisistaan. | EU 866/868 MHz -alueen säädösten noudattaminen: Käytä Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast tai Narrow Slow -asetuksia — ne on optimoitu EU:n SRD/868 MHz -alueille kapeammilla kaistanleveyksillä. | Kiinteät infrastruktuurilinkit: Käytä Short Turbo- tai Long Turbo -asetusta erillisille pisteestä pisteeseen -linkeille, joissa on hyvät antennit ja suora näköyhteys. | Sekaverkot: Pysy Long Fast -asetuksessa — se on yhteisön oletusasetus ja varmistaa yhteensopivuuden alueesi muiden käyttäjien kanssa. | . Kaikkien samalla kanavalla olevien radioiden on käytettävä samaa modeemiesiasetusta. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. Modeemiesiasetukset-taulukon kantama-arviot perustuvat tasaiseen maastoon ja vaatimattomiin antenneihin. Korkeuseroetu (mäki, rakennuksen katto) kasvattaa käytännön kantamaa huomattavasti. Hyvin sijoitettu Long Fast -asetusta käyttävä Router voi usein toimia paremmin kuin maan tasalla oleva Long Slow -asetusta käyttävä radio.

Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Pois | . | Yksityinen avain | Radiosi yksityinen avain (säilytä turvallisesti). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Suojaustaso | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Julkinen avain | Radiosi julkinen avain (vain luku) | Derived from the private key | . | Luo uusi yksityinen avain | Luo tälle radiolle uuden avainparin vahvistuksen jälkeen. Kaikkien vanhan avaimesi tunteneiden vertaisradioiden on opittava uusi avain | — | . | Palauta avaimet | Kirjoita varmuuskopioidut avaimet takaisin radioon (käytettävissä, kun varmuuskopio on olemassa) | — | . | Sarjaporttikonsoli | Serial console over the Stream API | Käytössä | . Lukitustila . Lukitustila salaa laitteen tallennustilan ja edellyttää tunnuslausetta jokaiselle yhteydelle. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Varoitus: Tunnuslausetta ei voi palauttaa. Jos kadotat sen, laite on tyhjennettävä sen palauttamiseksi, jolloin sen avaimet, kanavat ja asetukset poistuvat. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Tunnuslauseen lisäksi määrität rajat, joiden täyttyessä istunto päättyy automaattisesti: . | Kenttä | Mitä se tekee | . | Jäljellä olevat käynnistykset | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Tuntia vanhenemiseen saakka | Avatun tilan enimmäiskesto | . | Istunnon enimmäiskesto (minuuttia) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Kun lukitustila on käytössä, tässä lukee Aktiivinen – tallennustila salattu, tämä yhteys todennettu, kun yhteys on avattu, tai Aktiivinen – avaa tämä yhteys antamalla tunnuslause, kun sitä ei ole avattu. Lukitse nyt päättää nykyisen istunnon välittömästi. Toistuvat virheelliset tunnuslauseet rajoitetaan odotusajalla, ennen kuin voit yrittää uudelleen.

5228.title: Settings — Radio & User
5228.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5229.title: How these screens work
5229.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5230.title: User Settings
5230.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Beschrijving | Standaard | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Off | . | Long Name | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Short Name | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Empty | . | Niet berichtbaar | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Off | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5232.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Beschrijving | Standaard | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Coding Rate | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Frequency Override | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Frequency Slot | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Negeer MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Off | . | Overschrijf Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Off | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Off | . | Presets | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5238.title: Beveiligings Configuratie
5238.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Beschrijving | Standaard | . | Admin Sleutel | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Geen | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Debug Logs | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Off | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Beheerde modus | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Off | . | Privésleutel | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Publieke sleutel | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Seriële console | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5242.title: How these screens work
5242.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Празно | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Искључен | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. 5251.title: Сигурносна подешавања
5251.content: On Settings → Security. The screen is grouped into cards: Packet authenticity, Direct Message Key (your node’s key pair), Admin Keys, Logs, and Administration. | Setting | Опис | Подразумевано | . | Admin Key | Public keys permitted to administer this node remotely, up to three | Bez | . | Backup Keys | Save an encrypted backup of the node’s keys on this phone. Only for your own node, and not in the desktop app | — | . | Дебаг логови | Output live debug logging over serial, and view and export position-redacted node logs over Bluetooth | Искључен | . | Delete Key Backup | Remove the stored key backup from this phone | — | . | Управљани уређај | Locks the whole Configuration list, not just channels — every setting on the node becomes read-only and only an admin can change anything. Only selectable once an Admin Key is set | Искључен | . | Privatni ključ | Your node’s private key (handle securely). Shown redacted when you are viewing another node over remote admin — the firmware doesn’t send it | Generated by the node | . | Protection level | How unsigned packets are treated: Strict — Require authentication, Balanced — Prefer authenticated, or Compatible — Accept unsigned. Needs firmware that supports packet signing; Strict asks for confirmation | Compatible | . | Javni ključ | Your node’s public key (read-only) | Derived from the private key | . | Regenerate Private Key | Issues a new keypair for this node, behind a confirmation. Every peer that knew your old key must learn the new one | — | . | Restore Keys | Write the backed-up keys back to the node (available once a backup exists) | — | . | Серијска конзола | Serial console over the Stream API | On | . Lockdown Mode . Lockdown encrypts the device’s storage and requires a passphrase for each connection. It needs supporting firmware; the row doesn’t appear otherwise. ⚠️ Warning: There is no passphrase recovery. Losing it means erasing the device to get it back, which destroys its keys, channels and settings. Enabling it asks you to set and confirm a passphrase, and to acknowledge that it locks the debug (SWD) port on hardware where the lockout takes effect. That part isn’t reversible from the app. Turning lockdown off later decrypts your storage and reboots the device, but the port stays locked. Reopening it takes a full chip erase with a debug probe, which destroys everything on the device. Alongside the passphrase you set the limits that end a session automatically: . | Field | What it does | . | Boots remaining | How many device boots the unlocked state survives. Starts at 50 | . | Hours until expiry | Wall-clock lifetime of the unlocked state | . | Session cap (minutes) | A per-boot uptime cap on the unlocked state. 0, the default, means no cap | . Once active, the row reads Active — storage encrypted, this connection authenticated when unlocked, or Active — enter your passphrase to unlock this connection when not. Lock Now ends the current session immediately. Repeated wrong passphrases are rate-limited with a back-off before you can try again.

5254.title: Settings — Radio & User
5254.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5255.title: How these screens work
5255.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .

5256.title: User Settings
5256.content: User Profile . On Settings → User. The screen also shows the read-only Node ID and Hardware model. | Setting | Опис | Подразумевано | . | Licensed amateur radio (Ham) | Turn on if you hold an amateur radio license. Turning it on is staged behind a confirmation dialog, because licensed mode removes the channel encryption keys and sends all traffic as plaintext. On your own node it then relabels Long Name as Call sign (up to 7 characters) and adds a separate, optional Long Name that is appended to the call sign. Over remote admin the field stays Long Name | Искључен | . | Дуго име | The name your node broadcasts. Up to 24 bytes on firmware 2.8 or newer, and 39 on older firmware. To rename another node only on this device, see Display names | Set by the firmware | . | Кратко име | Up to four characters | Set by the firmware | . | Status Message | A short, public free-text status other nodes display alongside your node, up to 80 bytes, cleared with the ✕ in the field. The node broadcasts it to the mesh when you change it and again every 12 hours. Needs firmware 2.7.20 or newer, and is absent otherwise | Празно | . | Unmessageable | Marks the node as unmonitored or infrastructure, one nobody should try to message. This app shows it with an icon in the node list. Firmware 2.6.9 or newer is needed to change it | Искључен | . Applying changes . The footer appears as soon as you change something. Discard throws the change away, and the other button writes it to the node: it reads Save & restart on the screens the firmware applies with a reboot — Position, Network, Bluetooth, Security, and most module screens — and Save everywhere else. The status message is saved with the same Save, but it never reboots the node — and, like the rest of this screen, it can be edited on a remote node you administer. For your own node there is a shortcut while it is connected: touch & hold your node in the node list and choose Update status. Older firmware and a disconnected node have no shortcut — the field itself is still the way in.

5258.title: LoRA подешавања
5258.content: On Settings → LoRa. These settings decide where and how the node transmits. Region, preset and the manual modem settings are on the Options card. The rest are on Advanced. ⚠️ Important: Operating without the correct region may violate local radio regulations. See the region configuration guide on meshtastic.org for details. | Setting | Опис | Подразумевано | . | Bandwidth (kHz) | Manual mode only: the channel bandwidth in kHz, typed in directly. On the 2.4 GHz region the app offers a list of the bandwidths your node supports instead, headed by Default (812.5 kHz). A stored value that isn’t on that list shows as Unsupported and blocks saving until you pick a supported one | From preset | . | Стопа кодирања | Manual mode only: 5 to 8, the denominator of 4/n. More redundancy costs airtime | From preset | . | Coding Rate Override | Preset mode only, firmware 2.7.18 or newer: raises the preset’s coding rate for more error correction while keeping its bandwidth and spread factor. Only rates above the preset’s own are offered, and a preset already at 4/8 has none. Nodes on the same preset still hear each other, but every packet takes longer on air and uses more of the duty cycle. Switching to a preset that already meets the override resets it to the preset default | Preset default | . | Измена фреквенције | Overrides the computed operating frequency outright, in MHz. It doesn’t offset the calculated value. While it is 0 the field shows the computed frequency with Auto beside it | 0 (use calculated) | . | Фреквенцијски слот | Which slot within the region’s band to use. At 0 the region picks the slot, usually from the primary channel name, and the field shows that slot with Auto beside it | 0 (automatic) | . | Hop Limit | How many times a message may be repeated before it stops being forwarded, 0 to 7 | 3 | . | Игнориши MQTT | Drop packets that arrived from MQTT rather than over the air. The firmware turns this on for you whenever you set a region that has a duty-cycle limit — the EU bands, Thailand, and Ukraine 433 | Off, until you set a duty-cycle-limited region | . | OK to MQTT | Allow your packets to be forwarded to MQTT by gateways | Искључен | . | Override Duty Cycle | Ignores the region’s duty-cycle limit. Illegal in most regions; turn it on only where your license permits | Искључен | . | PA Fan Disabled | Turn off the power-amplifier fan. Shown only on hardware that has one | Искључен | . | Унапред подешено | Speed and range tradeoff, listed by full name such as Long Range - Fast. See Modem presets | Long Fast. When a node on firmware 2.8 or newer is first set to the United States region, the app picks Long Turbo | . | Регион | Regulatory region for frequency bands. You must set this before transmitting. On firmware 2.8 or newer, the first region set also creates the node’s identity key and gives it a new node number | Unset (must configure) | . | Појачање пријемника | Extra receive gain on SX126x radios; costs a little current | On | . | Фактор ширења | Manual mode only: 5 to 12. Higher spreads further but slower. On SX127x (RF95) radios the firmware doesn’t accept 5 or 6 and uses 11 instead | From preset | . | Трансмитер укључен | Turning this off makes the node receive-only | On | . | Transmit Power | In dBm. 0 uses the highest power legal for the region, which suits most nodes | 0 (region max) | . | Користи предефинисано подешавање | Turn it off to set Spread Factor, Coding Rate and Bandwidth by hand instead of taking them from the modem preset | On | . The preset list is also filtered to what your region legally permits, so a preset allowed in one region doesn’t appear in another. Changing region can therefore leave your current preset illegal — the app repairs it for you, switching to the region’s own default rather than leaving an unusable setting in place. The region list itself is filtered by what your firmware supports, so the regions added in 2.8 appear only on 2.8 or later, alongside whichever region the node already has set. Some regions are amateur radio allocations whose presets only licensed operators may use. On firmware 2.8 or newer the app knows which regions those are and grays the whole Presets list out until Licensed amateur radio (Ham) is turned on for the node you are configuring; the text under the field says so while it is grayed out. Modem presets . The Lite, Narrow, Medium Turbo, and Tiny presets need firmware 2.8 or newer — the app hides them on older nodes. This table uses the short names. The Presets dropdown spells each one out, such as Long Range - Fast, Short Range - Turbo and Lite - Slow. The SNR Limit values are negative on purpose. LoRa can decode signals below the noise floor, so a more-negative limit means the preset tolerates a weaker, noisier signal (more range). See How the Signal Meter Works for the full explanation. | Preset | Range | Брзина | SNR Limit | Best For | . | Short Turbo | ~1 km | 21.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Dense urban with line-of-sight; data-heavy applications | . | Short Fast | ~3 km | 10.9 kbps | −7.5 dB | Urban neighborhoods; buildings within a few blocks | . | Short Slow | ~5 km | 6.25 kbps | −10 dB | Suburban short-range; moderate building density | . | Medium Fast | ~5 km | 3.52 kbps | −12.5 dB | Suburban areas; moderate building density | . | Medium Slow | ~8 km | 1.95 kbps | −15 dB | Suburban/rural; moderate range with slower speed | . | Long Turbo | ~10 km | 1.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Similar range to Long Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; faster throughput | . | Long Fast | ~10 km | 1.1 kbps | −17.5 dB | General use (default) — balanced range and speed | . | Long Moderate | ~20 km | 0.34 kbps | −17.5 dB | Rural with some terrain; occasional use | . | Lite Fast | ~5 km | 1.76 kbps | −12.5 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Medium Fast | . | Lite Slow | ~10 km | 0.98 kbps | −15 dB | EU 866 MHz SRD band (125 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Narrow Fast | ~5 km | 2.28 kbps | −7.5 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); avoids interference with other devices | . | Narrow Slow | ~10 km | 1.30 kbps | −10 dB | EU 868 MHz band (62.5 kHz BW); comparable to Long Fast | . | Medium Turbo | ~5 km | 7.0 kbps | −12.5 dB | Like Medium Fast but with 500 kHz bandwidth; not legal in every region. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer | . | Tiny Fast | ~10 km | 0.68 kbps | −7.5 dB | Amateur bands that cap occupied bandwidth; these presets use 15.6 kHz. Needs firmware 2.8 or newer, an SX126x or SX127x radio, and a TCXO of ±5 ppm or better | . | Tiny Slow | ~20 km | 0.33 kbps | −10 dB | Same band restrictions as Tiny Fast, longer range. Same firmware, node, and TCXO requirements | . | Long Slow | ~30 km | 0.18 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Still selectable, but may be removed in a future firmware release | . | Very Long Slow | ~40+ km | 0.09 kbps | −20 dB | Deprecated. Firmware 2.6.5 and newer no longer support it | . Choosing a modem preset . The modem preset controls the fundamental tradeoff between range and data rate: . | Slower presets use more spreading, making signals decodable at weaker signal levels (lower SNR limit). This means longer range but fewer bytes per second. | Faster presets pack more data per transmission but require a stronger signal to decode. | . Practical guidance: . | Urban mesh (many nodes, short distances): Use Long Fast (default) or Short Fast. Higher speed means less airtime congestion when many nodes share the channel. | Rural/sparse mesh (few nodes, long distances): Use Long Moderate. Range matters more than speed when nodes are far apart. | EU 866/868 MHz regulatory compliance: Use Lite Fast, Lite Slow, Narrow Fast, or Narrow Slow — these are optimized for the EU SRD/868 MHz bands with narrower bandwidths. | Fixed infrastructure links: Use Short Turbo or Long Turbo for dedicated point-to-point links with good antennas and line-of-sight. | Mixed environments: Stick with Long Fast — it’s the community default and ensures compatibility with others in your area. | . All nodes on the same channel must use the same modem preset. Nodes with mismatched presets can’t communicate even if they share the same frequency and encryption key. The range estimates in the Modem Presets table assume flat terrain and modest antennas. Elevation advantage (hilltop, rooftop) dramatically increases effective range. A well-placed Router with Long Fast can often outperform a ground-level node with Long Slow.

5267.title: Settings — Radio & User
5267.content: Configure your node’s user identity, region and LoRa parameters, position and power behavior, network and Bluetooth connectivity, and security settings.

5268.title: How these screens work
5268.content: Everything here is on the Settings screen. User, LoRa, Channels and Security are listed there directly, under Configuration. Device, Position, Power, Network, Display and Bluetooth are one level down, under Settings → Device configuration. Network appears only on nodes with Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and Bluetooth only on nodes with Bluetooth. The Search settings field at the top of the Settings screen finds a setting by its name, its description, or a related term such as ttl for Hop Limit. Choosing a result opens the screen that holds the setting, scrolls to it, and highlights it for a moment. While you administer a remote node, the results leave out this phone’s own app settings. With no node connected, the screens still open and show the settings last read from your own node, under the line Connect to a radio to change these settings. The controls stay disabled until a node connects. Settings use standard preference controls — dropdowns, toggles, and sliders: . | Control | Screenshot | . | Dropdown | | . | Toggle | | . | Slider | | .
