7184.doc: Yksiköt, mittaus ja kieli- ja alueasetukset
7184.title: Yksiköt, mittaus ja kieli- ja alueasetukset
7184.content: Meshtastic-sovellus näyttää lämpötilat, etäisyydet, nopeudet ja ajat automaattisesti niissä yksiköissä, jotka laitteesi on määritetty käyttämään. Jos laitteesi asetukset eivät tarjoa haluamiasi yksiköitä, sovelluksen Yksiköt-asetus ohittaa ne.

7185.doc: Yksiköt, mittaus ja kieli- ja alueasetukset
7185.title: Kuinka se toimii
7185.content: Meshtastic nodes always transmit data in metric units (meters, °C, m/s, hPa, etc.). Kun sovellus vastaanottaa nämä tiedot, se muuntaa ja näyttää arvot laitteesi alueasetusten mukaisessa yksikköjärjestelmässä. Androidissa mittausasetukset määräytyvät järjestelmän Kieli ja alue -asetusten mukaan. Työpöytäversiossa (JVM) sovellus käyttää JVM:n oletus-Locale-asetusta. Yksiköt seuraavat laitteesi aluetta, ei näytön kieltä. Pelkkä kieli, kuten English, sovelluksen omasta Kieli-asetuksesta tai Androidin sovelluskohtaisesta kieliasetuksesta säilyttää laitteesi alueasetuksen. Kieli, jossa on oma alue, kuten English (Canada), ohittaa sen ja ottaa käyttöön kyseisen alueen yksiköt. On Android 16+, the system-wide Measurement system preference overrides the region for distance, speed, and the other measurements — but not for temperature, which keeps following the region. 💡 Vinkki: Oletusarvoisesti mitään ei tarvitse määrittää – muuta järjestelmän mittausjärjestelmäasetusta, niin kaikki Meshtasticin näkymät päivittyvät automaattisesti. Jos laitteesi ei tarjoa toimivaa alue- tai mittausjärjestelmäasetusta (joissakin valmistajien Android-versioissa näin on), määritä se sovelluksessa kohdassa Asetukset → Yksiköt.

7186.doc: Yksiköt, mittaus ja kieli- ja alueasetukset
7186.title: The node’s own screen is separate
7186.content: Settings → Device configuration → Display → Display Units configures the screen on the node, not the app. The 12 Hour Clock and Always point north settings do too, and all three apply to the node’s display only. Temperature on that screen has its own setting, Display Fahrenheit, on the node’s Telemetry module. See the Telemetry module reference on meshtastic.org. If your node list shows miles while the node’s screen shows kilometers, this is why: the two are set in different places. Changing the node’s setting never alters what the app displays. Katso laitteen asetuksia koskevat ohjeet Meshtasticin [Näytön asetukset] (https://meshtastic.org/docs/configuration/radio/display) -oppaasta.

7197.title: Units, Measurement & Locale
7197.content: The Meshtastic app automatically displays temperatures, distances, speeds, and times in the units your device is configured to use. If your device’s settings can’t express the units you want, an in-app Units setting overrides them.

7198.title: How It Works
7198.content: Meshtastic nodes always transmit data in metric units (meters, °C, m/s, hPa, etc.). When the app receives this data, it converts and displays values in whatever unit system your device’s locale specifies. On Android, your measurement preferences are determined by your system Language & Region settings. On Desktop (JVM), the app uses the JVM’s default Locale. Units follow your device’s region, not the display language. Plain languages — like English in the app’s own Language setting or Android’s per-app language — keep the region your device is set to. A choice that names a region of its own, like English (Canada), overrides it and brings that region’s units with it. On Android 16+, the system-wide Measurement system preference overrides the region for distance, speed, and the other measurements — but not for temperature, which keeps following the region. 💡 Tip: By default there is nothing to configure — change your system measurement preferences and every screen in Meshtastic updates automatically. If your device offers no working region or measurement setting (some manufacturer builds don’t), set Settings → Units in the app instead.

7225.title: Units, Measurement & Locale
7225.content: The Meshtastic app automatically displays temperatures, distances, speeds, and times in the units your device is configured to use. If your device’s settings can’t express the units you want, an in-app Units setting overrides them.

7226.title: How It Works
7226.content: Meshtastic nodes always transmit data in metric units (meters, °C, m/s, hPa, etc.). When the app receives this data, it converts and displays values in whatever unit system your device’s locale specifies. On Android, your measurement preferences are determined by your system Language & Region settings. On Desktop (JVM), the app uses the JVM’s default Locale. Units follow your device’s region, not the display language. Plain languages — like English in the app’s own Language setting or Android’s per-app language — keep the region your device is set to. A choice that names a region of its own, like English (Canada), overrides it and brings that region’s units with it. On Android 16+, the system-wide Measurement system preference overrides the region for distance, speed, and the other measurements — but not for temperature, which keeps following the region. 💡 Tip: By default there is nothing to configure — change your system measurement preferences and every screen in Meshtastic updates automatically. If your device offers no working region or measurement setting (some manufacturer builds don’t), set Settings → Units in the app instead.

7227.title: The node’s own screen is separate
7227.content: Settings → Device configuration → Display → Display Units configures the screen on the node, not the app. The 12 Hour Clock and Always point north settings do too, and all three apply to the node’s display only. Temperature on that screen has its own setting, Display Fahrenheit, on the node’s Telemetry module. See the Telemetry module reference on meshtastic.org. If your node list shows miles while the node’s screen shows kilometers, this is why: the two are set in different places. Changing the node’s setting never alters what the app displays. See the Display Config guide on meshtastic.org for the device-side options.

7281.title: Units, Measurement & Locale
7281.content: The Meshtastic app automatically displays temperatures, distances, speeds, and times in the units your device is configured to use. If your device’s settings can’t express the units you want, an in-app Units setting overrides them.

7282.title: How It Works
7282.content: Meshtastic nodes always transmit data in metric units (meters, °C, m/s, hPa, etc.). When the app receives this data, it converts and displays values in whatever unit system your device’s locale specifies. On Android, your measurement preferences are determined by your system Language & Region settings. On Desktop (JVM), the app uses the JVM’s default Locale. Units follow your device’s region, not the display language. Plain languages — like English in the app’s own Language setting or Android’s per-app language — keep the region your device is set to. A choice that names a region of its own, like English (Canada), overrides it and brings that region’s units with it. On Android 16+, the system-wide Measurement system preference overrides the region for distance, speed, and the other measurements — but not for temperature, which keeps following the region. 💡 Tip: By default there is nothing to configure — change your system measurement preferences and every screen in Meshtastic updates automatically. If your device offers no working region or measurement setting (some manufacturer builds don’t), set Settings → Units in the app instead.

7283.title: The node’s own screen is separate
7283.content: Settings → Device configuration → Display → Display Units configures the screen on the node, not the app. The 12 Hour Clock and Always point north settings do too, and all three apply to the node’s display only. Temperature on that screen has its own setting, Display Fahrenheit, on the node’s Telemetry module. See the Telemetry module reference on meshtastic.org. If your node list shows miles while the node’s screen shows kilometers, this is why: the two are set in different places. Changing the node’s setting never alters what the app displays. See the Display Config guide on meshtastic.org for the device-side options.

7284.title: Temperatura
7284.content: Temperature values from environment sensors are transmitted as °C and displayed based on your device’s temperature unit preference. | Your Setting | You See | . | Celsius | 22°C | . | Fahrenheit | 72°F | . This affects all temperature displays throughout the app: node environment telemetry, soil temperature, dew point, and telemetry chart axes. 7337.title: Units, Measurement & Locale
7337.content: The Meshtastic app automatically displays temperatures, distances, speeds, and times in the units your device is configured to use. If your device’s settings can’t express the units you want, an in-app Units setting overrides them.

7338.title: How It Works
7338.content: Meshtastic nodes always transmit data in metric units (meters, °C, m/s, hPa, etc.). When the app receives this data, it converts and displays values in whatever unit system your device’s locale specifies. On Android, your measurement preferences are determined by your system Language & Region settings. On Desktop (JVM), the app uses the JVM’s default Locale. Units follow your device’s region, not the display language. Plain languages — like English in the app’s own Language setting or Android’s per-app language — keep the region your device is set to. A choice that names a region of its own, like English (Canada), overrides it and brings that region’s units with it. On Android 16+, the system-wide Measurement system preference overrides the region for distance, speed, and the other measurements — but not for temperature, which keeps following the region. 💡 Tip: By default there is nothing to configure — change your system measurement preferences and every screen in Meshtastic updates automatically. If your device offers no working region or measurement setting (some manufacturer builds don’t), set Settings → Units in the app instead.

7339.title: The node’s own screen is separate
7339.content: Settings → Device configuration → Display → Display Units configures the screen on the node, not the app. The 12 Hour Clock and Always point north settings do too, and all three apply to the node’s display only. Temperature on that screen has its own setting, Display Fahrenheit, on the node’s Telemetry module. See the Telemetry module reference on meshtastic.org. If your node list shows miles while the node’s screen shows kilometers, this is why: the two are set in different places. Changing the node’s setting never alters what the app displays. See the Display Config guide on meshtastic.org for the device-side options.

7393.title: What’s New in the Docs
7393.content: October 2026 — Firmware Updates — What the Meshtastic nRF52 Bootloader does while the update drive is up, and where a node waits after a dropped Bluetooth update. October 2026 — Settings — Radio & User — Each configuration screen has its own section, settings use the app’s exact labels, and every table lists the default value. October 2026 — Firmware Updates — A node on firmware from 2.3.15 up to 2.5.14 stays connected behind a required-update screen, and the Connect tab flags a newer stable release. October 2026 — Messages & Channels — A failed message can be resent in place, and on firmware 2.8.1 or newer a direct message can show Delivered to recipient · proven. October 2026 — Desktop App — Site Planner computes coverage inside the app and adds it to the map as a layer. October 2026 — Map & Waypoints — The AR mesh view draws nodes and waypoints over the phone’s camera and turns you toward the one you are finding. September 2026 — Notifications — A page that lists every notification category, what each opens when tapped, when a message stays quiet, and what a message notification lets you do from the shade or a watch. September 2026 — Nodes — On firmware 2.8.1 or newer, nodes your node has not heard since its LoRa settings changed carry an orange marker, a Hide unheard nodes filter, and a banner whose Remove action deletes them after you confirm.

7394.title: Widget na domovské obrazovce
7394.content: On Android, Meshtastic provides two home screen widgets: . | Meshtastic shows live local statistics from your connected node. | Node Tracker follows one node you choose: its battery, signal, when it was last heard, how many hops away it is, and how far it is from your connected node. | . You can place as many of each as you like. Each Node Tracker remembers its own node.

7395.title: Lokální statistiky
7395.content: The Meshtastic widget displays the connected node’s current local stats: . | A node chip across the top, carrying the node’s short name in its own colors | Battery — the node’s battery level, or Powered when running on external power | ChUtil — využití kanálu (jak je kanál LoRa vytížený, v procentech) | AirUtil — the percentage of airtime this node used transmitting in the last hour | Provoz – pakety odeslané / přijaté a zaznamenané duplikáty | Relays — packets relayed and relay cancellations (shown when the node is relaying) | Diagnostics — a combined line carrying Noise (the background noise level in dBm), Bad (corrupt packets received), and Dropped (packets the node discarded). Bad and Dropped appear only once they are above zero, so a quiet node may show the noise reading alone | Heap — free versus total memory on the node, drawn as a bar | Uzly — počet uzlů online z celkového počtu známých uzlů | Uptime — how long the node has been running since its last reboot, shown beside Nodes | Aktualizováno – čas poslední aktualizace statistik, zobrazený v dolní části widgetu | . Klepnutím na widget otevřete aplikaci nebo pomocí tlačítka obnovení vyžádejte aktuální statistiky. ℹ️ Note: The values reflect the connected node. If the node disconnects, the widget replaces the stats with a status line: Disconnected, Connecting, or Device sleeping. Nezobrazuje poslední známé hodnoty.

7396.title: Node Tracker
7396.content: The Node Tracker widget shows one node from your node list: . | The node’s chip and long name | Battery: the node’s last reported battery level, or Powered on external power | Last heard: the time your connected node last heard it, or the date if it was more than a day ago | . Widen the widget to add a second column: . | SNR and RSSI: the signal of the node’s last packet, shown only when the node is heard directly rather than through other nodes or MQTT | Hops Away: how many hops away the node is, or Direct | Distance: how far the node is from your connected node. It appears only while you are connected and both nodes have a position | . When a node has not been heard within the last two hours, the widget dims its readings so they do not read as current. Tap the widget to open that node’s details in the app. After you disconnect from your node in the app, the widget keeps the tracked node’s last readings on screen, dimmed, until you reconnect. If your node list does not include the node you picked, because you removed it or connected to a different node, the widget says Node not found. Tap it to choose another node.

7397.title: Adding a Widget
7397.content: . | Dotkněte se prázdného místa na domovské obrazovce Androidu a podržte jej. | Tap Widgets, then find Meshtastic in the list. | Drag the Meshtastic (local stats) or Node Tracker widget to your home screen. | For a Node Tracker, pick the node to follow. Your favorites are listed first, then the most recently heard nodes; type in the search field to filter by name or node ID. Backing out without picking cancels the widget. | Podle potřeby změňte jeho velikost – rozložení se přizpůsobí dostupnému prostoru. | . To track a different node later, touch & hold the Node Tracker and choose the widget’s settings or reconfigure option. The exact wording depends on your launcher. ℹ️ Note: The widgets are Android-only. They are not available in the desktop app.

7430.content: The Meshtastic widget displays the connected node’s current local stats: . | A node chip across the top, carrying the node’s short name in its own colors | Battery — the node’s battery level, or Powered when running on external power | ChUtil：チャンネル利用率（LoRa チャンネルがどれだけ混雑しているかを割合で表示） | AirUtil — the percentage of airtime this node used transmitting in the last hour | Traffic：送受信したパケットと、検出した重複 | Relays — packets relayed and relay cancellations (shown when the node is relaying) | Diagnostics — a combined line carrying Noise (the background noise level in dBm), Bad (corrupt packets received), and Dropped (packets the node discarded). Bad and Dropped appear only once they are above zero, so a quiet node may show the noise reading alone | Heap — free versus total memory on the node, drawn as a bar | Nodes — how many nodes are online, out of the total known | Uptime — how long the node has been running since its last reboot, shown beside Nodes | Updated — the time the stats last refreshed, along the foot of the widget | . ウィジェットをタップするとアプリが開きます。更新コントロールを使うと、最新の統計を要求できます。 . ℹ️ Note: The values reflect the connected node. If the node disconnects, the widget replaces the stats with a status line: Disconnected, Connecting, or Device sleeping. It does not keep the last-known numbers on screen.

7431.doc: ホーム画面ウィジェット
7431.title: Node Tracker
7431.content: The Node Tracker widget shows one node from your node list: . | The node’s chip and long name | Battery: the node’s last reported battery level, or Powered on external power | Last heard: the time your connected node last heard it, or the date if it was more than a day ago | . Widen the widget to add a second column: . | SNR and RSSI: the signal of the node’s last packet, shown only when the node is heard directly rather than through other nodes or MQTT | Hops Away: how many hops away the node is, or Direct | Distance: how far the node is from your connected node. It appears only while you are connected and both nodes have a position | . When a node has not been heard within the last two hours, the widget dims its readings so they do not read as current. Tap the widget to open that node’s details in the app. After you disconnect from your node in the app, the widget keeps the tracked node’s last readings on screen, dimmed, until you reconnect. If your node list does not include the node you picked, because you removed it or connected to a different node, the widget says Node not found. Tap it to choose another node.

7432.doc: ホーム画面ウィジェット
7432.title: Adding a Widget
7432.content: . | Touch & hold an empty area of your Android home screen. | Tap Widgets, then find Meshtastic in the list. | Drag the Meshtastic (local stats) or Node Tracker widget to your home screen. | For a Node Tracker, pick the node to follow. Your favorites are listed first, then the most recently heard nodes; type in the search field to filter by name or node ID. Backing out without picking cancels the widget. | 必要に応じてサイズを変更します。レイアウトは利用可能なスペースに合わせて調整されます。 | . To track a different node later, touch & hold the Node Tracker and choose the widget’s settings or reconfigure option. The exact wording depends on your launcher. ℹ️ Note: The widgets are Android-only. They are not available in the desktop app.

7549.title: Local Stats
7549.content: The Meshtastic widget displays the connected node’s current local stats: . | A node chip across the top, carrying the node’s short name in its own colors | Battery — the node’s battery level, or Powered when running on external power | ChUtil — channel utilization (how busy the LoRa channel is, as a percentage) | AirUtil — the percentage of airtime this node used transmitting in the last hour | Traffic — packets transmitted / received, and duplicates seen | Relays — packets relayed and relay cancellations (shown when the node is relaying) | Diagnostics — a combined line carrying Noise (the background noise level in dBm), Bad (corrupt packets received), and Dropped (packets the node discarded). Bad and Dropped appear only once they are above zero, so a quiet node may show the noise reading alone | Heap — free versus total memory on the node, drawn as a bar | Nodes — how many nodes are online, out of the total known | Uptime — how long the node has been running since its last reboot, shown beside Nodes | Updated — the time the stats last refreshed, along the foot of the widget | . Tap the widget to open the app, or use its refresh control to request fresh stats. ℹ️ Note: The values reflect the connected node. If the node disconnects, the widget replaces the stats with a status line: Disconnected, Connecting, or Device sleeping. It does not keep the last-known numbers on screen.

7550.title: Node Tracker
7550.content: The Node Tracker widget shows one node from your node list: . | The node’s chip and long name | Battery: the node’s last reported battery level, or Powered on external power | Last heard: the time your connected node last heard it, or the date if it was more than a day ago | . Widen the widget to add a second column: . | SNR and RSSI: the signal of the node’s last packet, shown only when the node is heard directly rather than through other nodes or MQTT | Hops Away: how many hops away the node is, or Direct | Distance: how far the node is from your connected node. It appears only while you are connected and both nodes have a position | . When a node has not been heard within the last two hours, the widget dims its readings so they do not read as current. Tap the widget to open that node’s details in the app. After you disconnect from your node in the app, the widget keeps the tracked node’s last readings on screen, dimmed, until you reconnect. If your node list does not include the node you picked, because you removed it or connected to a different node, the widget says Node not found. Tap it to choose another node.

Backing out without picking cancels the widget. | Resize it as needed — the layout adapts to the available space. | . To track a different node later, touch & hold the Node Tracker and choose the widget’s settings or reconfigure option.
